# Changes on `open-architecture/deno-kcp--spec-bidder-and-bob-pds`

The requirement-level delta against `open-architecture/deno-kcp`, and what this branch realized.

## Requirements

### deploy-examples-atproto-market

- intent: "This context exists to pin down the deploy/examples/atproto/market example as an executable specification of what the kcp deno runtime must support: three peer services that reach each other only by cluster-local name over TLS, with identity and certificates supplied from outside the pod. It is the reference topology that exercises workspace creation, per-workspace API bindings, per-workspace RBAC, per-workspace OpenBao certificate authority selection, the provider's virtual DNS table and shim, and the TLS leaf injection path, and it exists so that a regression in any of those surfaces shows up as a failing verifier pod rather than as an untested assumption in the provider." -> "This context exists to pin down the deploy/examples/atproto/market example as an executable specification of what the kcp deno runtime must support: peer services that reach each other only by cluster-local name over TLS, with identity and certificates supplied from outside the pod, and a market bidder that reaches those same peers the same way. It is the reference topology that exercises workspace creation, per-workspace API bindings, per-workspace RBAC, per-workspace OpenBao certificate authority selection, the provider's virtual DNS table and shim, and the TLS leaf injection path, and it exists so that a regression in any of those surfaces shows up as a failing verifier pod rather than as an untested assumption in the provider. The example carries its own live acceptance, accept.sh, so that it is proven by bringing the whole topology up and reaching it, not only by decoding its manifests and fitting them to the schemas."
- added `r.acceptance-survives-a-stalled-provider` (MUST): "accept.sh must survive a provider that comes up, logs that it is waiting for its APIExport virtual workspace endpoints, and then reconciles nothing: every object apply.sh applies stays without a status and apply.sh fails on its first wait. After the provider is started and apply.sh returns, accept.sh must detect that state within a bounded window -- no OpenBao object in any workspace carries status.ready true and no DenoPod exists in any workspace -- and, when no workload exists yet, stop the provider, start it again, and run apply.sh again. It must make at least two and at most three attempts, print which attempt it is on, and record each attempt's apply.sh exit code. It must never restart the provider once a DenoPod exists, because the workloads are children of the provider and stopping it would orphan them."
- added `r.apply-includes-bob-and-bidder` (MUST): "apply.sh names the workspaces global relay alice bob, requires atproto-market/hono-bidder (as well as hono-plc, hono-atproto-relay and hono-pds) in its preflight check, generates a PDS key for bob and a key for the bidder, each distinct from alice's and each overridable by BOB_PDS_PRIVATE_KEY_HEX and BIDDER_PRIVATE_KEY_HEX, substitutes them for __BOB_PDS_PRIVATE_KEY_HEX__ and __BIDDER_PRIVATE_KEY_HEX__, applies 15-openbao-bob.yaml with the other authorities, applies 60-bob-pds.yaml before 70-bidder.yaml, and reports the phase and readiness of both pds and bidder in its final summary."
- added `r.arch-data-lists-bob` (SHOULD): "The open-architecture overlay data ov.market-workspaces in .tools/open-architecture/arch.yaml lists root:bob alongside root:global, root:relay and root:alice, so validate.py and 00-workspaces.yaml agree."
- added `r.bidder-pod` (MUST): "The bob workspace runs DenoPod bidder in namespace default under the deno-runner service account with restartPolicy Always, the denopod.deno.computer/run finalizer, SERVICE_ENTRY <ORG_ROOT>/atproto-market/hono-bidder/mod.ts (apply.sh rewrites the /home/johnandersen777/src/publicdomainrelay-kcp prefix), SERVICE_CWD <ORG_ROOT>/atproto-market, SERVICE_ARGS ["--serve-addr","127.0.0.1","--serve-port","2586","--plc-directory-url","https://plc.default.global.svc.kcp.local","--relay-url","https://relay.default.relay.svc.kcp.local","--skip-qr","--no-ingress-proxy","--compute-provider-deno-worker"] (the deno-worker compute provider is the only one that needs no cloud credential), SERVICE_DENO_FLAGS ["--unstable-kv"], SERVICE_TLS true, SERVICE_ENV {"PORT":"2586","HOSTNAME":"127.0.0.1","REPO_PRIVATE_KEY_HEX":"__BIDDER_PRIVATE_KEY_HEX__"} (PORT and HOSTNAME are what the provider advertises for bidder.default.bob.svc.kcp.local, because the bidder names its listener --serve-port and the name table only reads --port or PORT), and a readiness probe that resolves bidder.default.bob.svc.kcp.local and requests /oauth-client-metadata.json. It lives in root:bob because it is bob's market participant: it shares bob's OpenBao authority, service account and workspace identity with bob's PDS and reaches the market through the same virtual DNS table."
- added `r.bidder-supervisor-script` (MUST): "The bidder pod's script writes the injected KCP_CA_BUNDLE to ca.pem and sets DENO_CERT to it, prepends KCP_SHIM to the Deno flags as --preload, spawns the entry module as a child process with stdin null and inherited stdio, and writes the child exitCode to result.json. It must NOT write tls.crt or tls.key and must NOT append --tls-cert-file or --tls-key-file to the child argv: hono-bidder's cli-args-env declares no such options and its parser rejects unknown flags, so the bidder consumes only the trust bundle even though SERVICE_TLS is true."
- added `r.bob-pds-pod` (MUST): "The bob workspace runs DenoPod pds in namespace default under the deno-runner service account with restartPolicy Always, the denopod.deno.computer/run finalizer, SERVICE_TLS true, --unstable-kv in SERVICE_DENO_FLAGS, port 2585 (which collides with no other service: alice uses 2583, the relay 2584 and the PLC 2587), PDS_PUBLIC_HOSTNAME pds.default.bob.svc.kcp.local, PDS_PLC_DIRECTORY_URL pointed at the global PLC name, PDS_CRAWLERS pointed at the relay name, PDS_SUBSCRIBE_REPOS_FORMAT json, and PDS_PRIVATE_KEY_HEX in SERVICE_ENV as a key distinct from alice's (__BOB_PDS_PRIVATE_KEY_HEX__), so the two PDS identities differ."
- added `r.four-workspaces-at-root` (MUST): "The example creates exactly the four workspaces global, relay, alice and bob, each with spec.type.name denoruntime and spec.type.path root."
- added `r.live-acceptance-script` (MUST): "deploy/examples/atproto/market/accept.sh is the live acceptance of this example: it brings the whole market up in a throwaway state directory and exits non-zero unless every workload is up and reachable. It is bash with set -euo pipefail; ACCEPT_ROOT (default a fresh mktemp -d) is the one directory it owns, and an EXIT trap stops everything it started and removes that directory. It never stops or touches a kcp, kine or OpenBao it did not start. It asks the kernel for three free 127.0.0.1 ports, for kcp, kine and OpenBao, instead of pinning any, so it cannot collide with another instance on the machine. It starts kcp with ROOT=$ACCEPT_ROOT/kcp and KCP_SECURE_PORT and KINE_ENDPOINT set to two of those ports through deploy/start-kcp.sh; installs the provider with KUBECONFIG_PATH=$ACCEPT_ROOT/kcp/admin.kubeconfig through deploy/install-provider.sh; builds ./cmd/deno-kcp-provider into $ACCEPT_ROOT; starts OpenBao with OPENBAO_DIR=$ACCEPT_ROOT/openbao and OPENBAO_LISTEN on the third port through deploy/start-openbao.sh; and runs the provider with --kubeconfig, --openbao-addr http://<openbao port>, --openbao-token root and RUNS_DIR=$ACCEPT_ROOT/runs. It then runs deploy/examples/atproto/market/apply.sh with ORG_ROOT the repository parent, KUBECONFIG the kcp admin kubeconfig, OPENBAO_LISTEN the same address, START_OPENBAO=0, a bounded WAIT_SECONDS, and KEY_FILE, BOB_KEY_FILE and BIDDER_KEY_FILE under $ACCEPT_ROOT. When apply.sh returns, whether it succeeded or not, accept.sh reads every DenoPod from kcp with kubectl and prints one line per check, each with its result and the decisive evidence: apply.sh exited 0; DenoPod plc in root:global, relay in root:relay, pds in root:alice, pds in root:bob and bidder in root:bob each reached phase Running and report ready true; DenoPod verifier in root:alice reached the terminal phase Succeeded; bob pds answers on its own name, which the provider proves with its readiness probe through the shim (kcpdns pds.default.bob.svc.kcp.local /xrpc/_health) and the host proves by fetching the same path from outside with curl https://127.0.0.1:2585/xrpc/_health; the bidder answers on bidder.default.bob.svc.kcp.local /oauth-client-metadata.json and on http://127.0.0.1:2586/oauth-client-metadata.json. The host check names the scheme the listener actually speaks, and the two are not the same. The PDS in root:bob serves TLS -- its supervisor script writes the injected leaf and appends --tls-cert-file and --tls-key-file -- so its host check is https, because an http:// fetch of a TLS listener is not a check of anything and must not be written. The bidder serves plain HTTP on its port: SERVICE_TLS is true for it too, but its supervisor script must not append the TLS flags, because hono-bidder declares no such options and its parser rejects unknown ones, so the bidder consumes only the trust bundle and its listener is not the TLS one; its host check is therefore http://, and an https:// fetch of a plain listener fails the same way round. The readiness probe of the provider is the one that does not care, because it tries https and then http. http_code reports the status curl printed, and prints 000 exactly once when the fetch failed rather than appending a second fallback. And the five long-running pods are still Running with ready true when they are read a second time at least ten seconds later, so a pod that dies after startup fails the run. It prints a final table naming every check and its result, prints the tail of the provider log and the status of the failing pod when a check fails, and exits 0 only when every check passed."
- changed `r.openbao-object-per-workspace` (codeRefs, text): "Each workspace applies one OpenBao object named openbao in namespace default, carrying the finalizer openbao.deno.computer/namespace and naming the OpenBao namespace that serves it: global.default, relay.default, alice.default and bob.default respectively."
- added `r.rbac-covers-bob` (MUST): "apply.sh applies 10-rbac.yaml in root:bob as it does in every workspace, and every DenoPod in bob (pds and bidder) names the deno-runner service account. No new ClusterRole is added, because deno-runner-read-pods already grants get and list on denopods."
- added `r.readme-lists-bob-and-bidder` (MUST): "README.md's service table adds root:bob DenoPod/pds (hono-pds, port 2585, pds.default.bob.svc.kcp.local) and root:bob DenoPod/bidder (hono-bidder, port 2586, bidder.default.bob.svc.kcp.local), its OpenBao table adds root:bob OpenBao/openbao bob.default (15-openbao-bob.yaml), its prose says four workspaces, and its ceilings note that the bidder registers with an XRPC dispatcher, so it needs one reachable."
- removed `r.three-workspaces-at-root` (MUST)
- added `r.verifier-waits-for-its-peers` (MUST): "apply.sh must not create the verifier after a fixed sleep. It must instead wait, with the same bounded WAIT_SECONDS deadline it uses elsewhere, until the peers the verifier reaches are observable -- DenoPod pds in root:alice reports phase Running and ready true, which is the provider's own proof that pds.default.alice.svc.kcp.local resolves through the virtual DNS table and answers on /xrpc/_health -- and only then apply 50-verifier.yaml. When the deadline passes without that pod becoming ready, apply.sh must say so on stderr and still create the verifier, so the run reports the failure instead of hanging. A fixed sleep before a pod whose restartPolicy is Never is not a wait for anything and must not be written."

### internal-provider

- added `r.watch-cache-keys-every-workspace` (MUST): "The provider watches every workspace through one wildcard informer, and the same namespace and name can exist in more than one workspace -- a DenoPod named pds in namespace default exists in root:alice and in root:bob. The watch cache must key every object by its logical cluster as well as its namespace and name, so that two such objects are two independent cache entries. Both survive an informer re-list, both are returned by allPods and so appear in the virtual DNS table of every pod, and each is read back by a Ref that names its own workspace. A workload must never be evicted from the cache, dropped from the DNS table or skipped by the reconcile loop because another workspace holds an object with the same namespace and name; a DenoPod that is not ready must keep being reconciled and re-probed on its own key until it is ready or reaches a terminal phase."
- added `r.watch-cache-keys-every-workspace-test` (MUST): "An offline unit test inserts two DenoPods that share a namespace and a name but carry different kcp.io/cluster annotations into the watch cache and asserts that allPods returns both and that ReadPod resolves each one from its own workspace. The test must fail when the cache keys objects by namespace and name alone."

### test-integration

- intent: "This context exists to hold the one test package that proves deno-kcp works against real infrastructure and against the checked-in examples. It separates what can be verified from the repository alone (offline_test.go, examples.go) from what needs a running kcp, kine, deno and policy-engine (live_test.go, fixture_test.go) from what additionally needs the pinned OpenBao (bao_test.go, openbao_live_test.go), so the cheap checks run everywhere and the expensive ones are gated behind explicit opt-in. The fixture layer exists so that every live test describes intent in terms of typed Kubernetes objects and named expectations rather than raw HTTP, and so the OpenBao version certificates are issued by is the one the repository pins, never whatever binary happens to be on PATH." -> "This context exists to hold the one test package that proves deno-kcp works against real infrastructure and against the checked-in examples. It separates what can be verified from the repository alone (offline_test.go, examples.go) from what needs a running kcp, kine, deno and policy-engine (live_test.go, fixture_test.go) from what additionally needs the pinned OpenBao (bao_test.go, openbao_live_test.go), so the cheap checks run everywhere and the expensive ones are gated behind explicit opt-in. The fixture layer exists so that every live test describes intent in terms of typed Kubernetes objects and named expectations rather than raw HTTP, and so the OpenBao version certificates are issued by is the one the repository pins, never whatever binary happens to be on PATH. The example registry covers every kcp-kind manifest the repository ships, including the atproto market manifests under deploy/examples/atproto/market, so the offline tier decodes and schema-fits them with no cluster."
- added `r.market-examples-are-registered` (MUST): "The offline example registry covers the atproto market manifests. exampleFiles() in test/integration/examples.go carries an entry for every kcp-kind manifest under deploy/examples/atproto/market -- 15-openbao-global.yaml, 15-openbao-relay.yaml, 15-openbao-alice.yaml, 15-openbao-bob.yaml, 20-global-plc.yaml, 30-relay-relay.yaml, 40-alice-pds.yaml, 50-verifier.yaml, 60-bob-pds.yaml and 70-bidder.yaml -- with File holding the manifest's path relative to deploy/examples (e.g. atproto/market/70-bidder.yaml), and loadExampleFile joining that path onto localExamples(). exampleFilesOnDisk() walks deploy/examples recursively and returns the same relative paths. The two non-kcp manifests 00-workspaces.yaml and 10-rbac.yaml are declared non-examples by name in examples.go, and TestExampleInventoryMatchesDisk subtracts them from the disk walk so the inventory still agrees with disk. TestEveryExampleDecodesFromDisk and TestExamplesFitTheInstalledSchemas then decode and schema-fit the market manifests with the existing DenoPod and OpenBao entries and the existing denopod and openbao APIResourceSchemas."

### third-party-openbao

- intent: "" -> "This context exists to mark the boundary of the vendored upstream OpenBao tree inside deno-kcp, so that readers and tools do not confuse it with deno-kcp's first-party OpenBao handling in internal/provider. It records that the copies under third_party/openbao are upstream sources carried alongside the repository, together with the two golangci-lint configurations and the publiccode.yml that travel with them, and it records that the tree exposes no interfaces of its own to the deno-kcp module. It is a containment and provenance note rather than a behavioral contract: the renames and edits to make upstream OpenBao usable by deno-kcp happen in the first-party packages, not here."
- added `r.golangci-lint-configs` (MUST): "The vendored tree ships both its base lint configuration and a separate deprecations lint configuration, as third_party/openbao/.golangci.yml and third_party/openbao/.golangci.deprecations.yml."
- added `r.main-entrypoint` (MUST): "The vendored tree has a Go main package entry point at third_party/openbao/main.go."
- added `r.no-exported-interfaces` (MAY): "The vendored tree exports no interfaces of its own into the deno-kcp module; OpenBao handling in deno-kcp lives in the first-party internal/provider package instead."
- added `r.publiccode-metadata` (SHOULD): "The vendored tree keeps its upstream publiccode.yml project metadata alongside the sources."
- added `r.vendored-openbao-tree` (MUST): "The repository carries a vendored copy of OpenBao under third_party/openbao, kept apart from first-party deno-kcp packages."

### third-party-openbao-api

- intent: "" -> "This context exists to pin down how a caller authenticates against OpenBao credential backends and manages tokens from the Go API client, so that the Auth/AuthMethod seam and the MFA paths are described exactly as the vendored code implements them. It names the client entry point (Client.Auth), the delegation contract every backend satisfies (AuthMethod.Login), the MFA login and validation calls, and the token create accessor, so that the observed exports and their obligations are captured rather than inferred."
- added `r.auth-entry-point` (MUST): "The credential-backend API client is obtained by calling Client.Auth(), which returns an *Auth bound to that client."
- added `r.auth-login-delegates` (MUST): "Auth.Login takes an AuthMethod and delegates the actual credential exchange to that method's Login, returning its *Secret or error."
- added `r.authmethod-seam` (MUST): "Every credential backend integrates by implementing the AuthMethod interface, whose only method is Login(ctx context.Context, client *Client) (*Secret, error)."
- added `r.mfa-login-creds` (MUST): "Auth.MFALogin accepts an AuthMethod plus variadic MFA credential strings and selects the single-phase or two-phase MFA flow accordingly."
- added `r.mfa-validate` (MUST): "Auth.MFAValidate validates a given MFA secret against a payload map and returns the resulting *Secret or error."
- added `r.sys-mfa-validate` (SHOULD): "Sys.MFAValidate takes a requestID and payload map and forwards to the context-aware MFA validate call with context.Background()."
- added `r.token-auth-accessor` (MUST): "Auth.Token() returns a *TokenAuth carrying the same underlying client, giving access to token create operations."
- added `r.token-create-context` (MUST): "TokenAuth.Create forwards to TokenAuth.CreateWithContext using context.Background(), so the context-aware variant remains the single implementation point."
- added `r.two-phase-mfa-contract` (MUST): "The two-phase MFA login path calls AuthMethod.Login and, when the returned secret is nil, lacks Auth, or lacks MFARequirement, appends the warning "expected secret to contain MFARequirements" to the secret and returns the error "assumed two-phase MFA login, returned secret is missing MFARequirements"."

### third-party-openbao-api-auth-approle

- intent: "" -> "This context exists to describe the vendored OpenBao AppRole auth-method package that deno-kcp carries under `third_party/openbao`, so its public surface (constructor, functional options, `Login`) and its documented behavior (single secret-ID source, late resolution of file and environment values, bounded file read, optional wrapping-token unwrap, write to `auth/<mountPath>/login`) are recorded as requirements rather than re-derived from source on each change. It anchors the contract other parts of the repository rely on when authenticating to OpenBao with a role ID and secret ID, and it marks the package as upstream code whose behavior is already exercised by its own tests."
- added `r.auth-method-interface` (MUST): "AppRoleAuth satisfies api.AuthMethod, asserted at compile time with var _ api.AuthMethod = (*AppRoleAuth)(nil)."
- added `r.constructor-requires-role-id` (MUST): "NewAppRoleAuth returns the error "no role ID provided for login" when roleID is the empty string."
- added `r.constructor-requires-secret-id` (MUST): "NewAppRoleAuth returns the error "no secret ID provided for login" when secretID is nil."
- added `r.default-mount-path` (MUST): "NewAppRoleAuth sets mountPath to the constant defaultMountPath, which is "approle"; WithMountPath overrides it."
- added `r.file-read-bounded-and-trimmed` (MUST): "readSecretIDFromFile reads at most 1000 bytes through io.LimitReader and trims exactly one trailing newline with strings.TrimSuffix, returning wrapped errors "unable to open file containing secret ID: %w" and "unable to read secret ID: %w"."
- added `r.login-empty-env-var-fails` (MUST): "AppRoleAuth.Login fails when the configured environment variable holds an empty value, reporting "secret ID was specified with an environment variable %q with an empty value"."
- added `r.login-nil-context-defaulted` (MUST): "AppRoleAuth.Login replaces a nil context with context.Background() before making any client call."
- added `r.login-option-errors-wrapped` (MUST): "NewAppRoleAuth applies each LoginOption to the new AppRoleAuth and returns a wrapped error "error with login option: %w" if any option returns non-nil."
- added `r.login-resolves-secret-id-late` (MUST): "AppRoleAuth.Login resolves the secret ID at login time, preferring the file source, then the environment variable source, then the plaintext string; file and environment values are read late so the underlying value may change between construction and login."
- added `r.login-write-path` (MUST): "AppRoleAuth.Login writes the map {role_id, secret_id} to the path auth/<mountPath>/login using client.Logical().WriteWithContext and returns the resulting *api.Secret, wrapping failures as "unable to log in with app role auth: %w"."
- added `r.secret-id-single-source` (MUST): "SecretID.validate requires at least one of FromFile, FromEnv or FromString to be set, and rejects more than one source with the error "only one source for the secret ID should be specified"; NewAppRoleAuth wraps a failure as "invalid secret ID: %w"."
- added `r.third-party-vendored` (SHOULD): "The package is vendored upstream OpenBao code carrying the HashiCorp copyright header and the MPL-2.0 SPDX license identifier, and its behavior is exercised by TestLogin in approle_test.go."
- added `r.wrapping-token-unwrap` (MUST): "WithWrappingToken sets the unwrap flag, and AppRoleAuth.Login then calls client.Logical().UnwrapWithContext with the resolved value and uses the unwrapped token's secret_id field, failing with "unable to unwrap response wrapping token: %w" on error."

### third-party-openbao-api-auth-jwt

- intent: "" -> "This context exists to describe the JWT auth method of the embedded OpenBao client library that deno-kcp carries under third_party, so that the role-based login path used against an OpenBao server has a written contract independent of the surrounding vendored tree. It records how a JWTAuth value is validated and assembled, how options mutate it, and where the token comes from, so callers can rely on construction either failing fast with a named error or yielding a JWTAuth ready to log in."
- added `r.default-mount-path` (MUST): "New must initialize the JWTAuth mountPath to DefaultMountPath before applying any option."
- added `r.login-signature` (MUST): "JWTAuth.Login must take a context and an OpenBao api.Client and return an api.Secret together with an error."
- added `r.mount-path-non-empty` (MUST): "New must return ErrInvalidMountPath when the mountPath is empty after the options are applied."
- added `r.new-requires-role-name` (MUST): "New must return ErrNoRoleName when roleName is the empty string."
- added `r.option-signature` (MUST): "Option must be a func of a single *JWTAuth argument returning an error, so every option constructor composes through New."
- added `r.options-applied-in-order` (MUST): "New must apply each Option in the order given and return the option's error immediately, without returning a JWTAuth, when an option fails."
- added `r.token-or-path-required` (MUST): "New must return ErrNoToken when both token and tokenPath are empty after the options are applied."
- added `r.with-mount-path-sets-mount` (MUST): "WithMountPath must return an Option that sets the JWTAuth mount path to the given path and returns a nil error."
- added `r.with-token-from-env-reads-env` (MUST): "WithTokenFromEnv must return an Option that sets the JWTAuth token to the value of the named environment variable read with os.Getenv."
- added `r.with-token-from-path-sets-path` (MUST): "WithTokenFromPath must return an Option that sets the JWTAuth token path to the given path and returns a nil error."
- added `r.with-token-sets-token` (MUST): "WithToken must return an Option that sets the JWTAuth token to the given string and returns a nil error."

### third-party-openbao-api-auth-kubernetes

- intent: "" -> "The context exists to specify the Kubernetes auth method client helper so that callers and reimplementations know the exact constructor contract, option semantics, error strings, and login entry point. It pins down which behaviors are required of NewKubernetesAuth and of each LoginOption so that the Kubernetes backend login can be constructed and exercised against an *api.Client without reading the source. It also records that LoginOption here is a per-package type, not shared with the approle, ldap, or userpass packages."
- added `r.default-mount-path` (MUST): "NewKubernetesAuth must initialize the new KubernetesAuth with mountPath set to defaultMountPath before any LoginOption is applied."
- added `r.default-token-file-fallback` (MUST): "When no option has supplied a service account token, NewKubernetesAuth must read the token from defaultServiceAccountTokenPath and fail with "error reading service account token from default location: %w" if that read fails."
- added `r.login-uses-client` (MUST): "KubernetesAuth.Login must accept a context.Context and an *api.Client and return an *api.Secret, performing the Kubernetes auth login against the configured mount path and role."
- added `r.mount-path-option` (MUST): "WithMountPath must return a LoginOption that sets the mount path on the passed *KubernetesAuth and returns a nil error."
- added `r.options-applied-in-order` (MUST): "NewKubernetesAuth must call each supplied LoginOption in the order given, passing the instantiated *KubernetesAuth, and must return a nil result wrapped as "error with login option: %w" when an option returns a non-nil error."
- added `r.role-name-required` (MUST): "NewKubernetesAuth must reject an empty roleName by returning the error "no role name was provided" and a nil *KubernetesAuth, instead of returning a partially built struct."
- added `r.token-env-option` (MUST): "WithServiceAccountTokenEnv must read the named environment variable and return the error "service account token was specified with an environment variable with an empty value" when the variable is empty; otherwise it must store the value as the service account token and return nil."
- added `r.token-literal-option` (MUST): "WithServiceAccountToken must return a LoginOption that stores the supplied JWT directly as the service account token on the KubernetesAuth."
- added `r.token-path-option` (MUST): "WithServiceAccountTokenPath must return a LoginOption that records the given path as the location to read the service account token from."

### third-party-openbao-api-auth-ldap

- intent: "" -> "This context documents the vendored OpenBao LDAP authentication helper so its contract stays pinned to the code that ships in-tree. It exists because the file is third-party code copied into the repository rather than imported: the surrounding project depends on the exact behavior of NewLDAPAuth, LDAPAuth.Login, Password, LoginOption, and WithMountPath, and any local patch or upgrade must preserve the validation errors, the password-source precedence, the default mount path, and the write path that the rest of the tree relies on. The spec records those obligations, plus the compile-time api.AuthMethod assertion and the test file, so drift is visible."
- added `r.default-mount-path` (MUST): "NewLDAPAuth must initialize the LDAPAuth mount path to the defaultMountPath constant, whose value is "ldap"."
- added `r.implements-api-auth-method` (MUST): "LDAPAuth must satisfy the api.AuthMethod interface, asserted at compile time by a package-level assignment from (*LDAPAuth)(nil)."
- added `r.login-nil-context-default` (MUST): "LDAPAuth.Login must substitute context.Background() when ctx is nil, so the login call always carries a non-nil context."
- added `r.login-options-applied-in-order` (MUST): "NewLDAPAuth must apply each LoginOption to the constructed LDAPAuth in the order given, and must wrap any option error as "error with login option: %w" and return no LDAPAuth."
- added `r.login-password-env-empty-rejected` (MUST): "LDAPAuth.Login must read the env-var branch with os.Getenv and must fail with "password was specified with an environment variable with an empty value" when that variable is unset or empty."

### third-party-openbao-github-actions-set-up-go

- intent: "" -> "This context exists to pin down the contract of the vendored OpenBao workflow helper that sets up Go with a shared module cache, so the surrounding repository can rely on its inputs, outputs, cache key derivation, and cache-miss behavior without re-reading the YAML. It records the deliberate caching decisions encoded in the file: caching is left to this action rather than to actions/setup-go, the cache is cross-OS and lookup-only when no-restore is set, and no partial restore keys are used because GitHub caps repository caches at 10 GB and the same cache budget also holds Go test timing results."
- added `r.accept-no-restore-input` (MUST): "The action must declare a boolean input named no-restore, described as whether to restore the Go module cache on a cache hit, with default false."
- added `r.cache-budget-rationale` (SHOULD): "The caching strategy should stay within GitHub's 10 GB per-repository cache limit, which this repository also spends on Go test timing results, so the exact-key, no-partial-restore approach is preserved to keep upload time, download time, and storage size minimal."
- added `r.cache-uses-exact-key` (MUST): "The actions/cache step must use path ${{ steps.metadata.outputs.cache-path }} and key ${{ steps.metadata.outputs.cache-key }} and must not specify any partial restore keys."
- added `r.composite-run-surface` (MUST): "The action must run using composite and order its steps as go-version, actions/setup-go, metadata, cache-modules, then the conditional module download, with shell bash on every run step."
- added `r.cross-os-cache-archive` (MUST): "The actions/cache step, pinned at v6.1.0, must set enableCrossOsArchive to true."
- added `r.derive-go-version-from-file` (MUST): "The go-version step must run bash that reads ./.go-version and writes its contents to the go-version step output via $GITHUB_OUTPUT, and actions/setup-go must receive that value as go-version rather than a hard-coded version."
- added `r.disable-setup-go-caching` (MUST): "The actions/setup-go step, pinned at v7.0.0, must be invoked with cache set to false because the action uses its own caching strategy."
- added `r.download-modules-on-cache-miss` (MUST): "A step named Download go modules, guarded by if: steps.cache-modules.outputs.cache-hit != 'true' and running bash, must iterate over every file named go.mod found under the tree and, in each containing directory via pushd/popd, run go list ./..., go list -test ./..., and go mod download."
- added `r.export-cache-key-output` (MUST): "The action must publish a cache-key output, described as the Go modules cache key, whose value is ${{ steps.metadata.outputs.cache-key }}."
- added `r.export-cache-path-output` (MUST): "The action must publish a cache-path output, described as the GOMODCACHE path, whose value is ${{ steps.metadata.outputs.cache-path }}."
- added `r.export-go-version-output` (MUST): "The action must publish a go-version output, described as the version of Go in the .go-version file, whose value is ${{ steps.go-version.outputs.go-version }}."
- added `r.lookup-only-bound-to-input` (MUST): "The actions/cache step must set lookup-only to ${{ inputs.no-restore }} so a cache hit can be detected without restoring when requested."
- added `r.metadata-outputs-path-and-key` (MUST): "The metadata bash step must write cache-path as the result of go env GOMODCACHE and cache-key as the literal prefix go-modules- immediately followed by ${{ hashFiles('**/go.sum') }} into $GITHUB_OUTPUT."

### third-party-openbao-internal-audit

- intent: "" -> "This context exists to fix the contract of the audit package as a stable boundary between audit device backends and the rest of the server: a device supplies a Backend and a Formatter, the formatter serialises requests and responses into an AuditFormatWriter, and the hashing layer guarantees that secrets, tokens and potentially sensitive values are salted or HMAC'd before they leave the process. It is written so that the formatting and hashing behaviour cannot drift silently, because audit output is the forensic record and a leak or an unverifiable field is unrecoverable. The exported names, signatures and the required test files below are the parts that other packages and downstream devices depend on."
- added `r.audit-entry-structs` (MUST): "The formatted payload must be described by AuditRequestEntry and AuditResponseEntry wrapping AuditRequest and AuditResponse, with AuditAuth, AuditSecret, AuditResponseWrapInfo, AuditPolicyResults, PolicyInfo and AuditNamespace carrying the hashed auth, secret, wrap, policy and namespace fields."
- added `r.audit-format-writer` (MUST): "A serialisation format must implement AuditFormatWriter: WriteRequest(io.Writer, *AuditRequestEntry) error, WriteResponse(io.Writer, *AuditResponseEntry) error, and Salt(context.Context) (*salt.Salt, error)."
- added `r.audit-formatter` (MUST): "AuditFormatter must implement Formatter by formatting requests and responses from a logical.LogInput into the writer, and NewTemporaryFormatter(format, prefix string) *AuditFormatter must return an AuditFormatter for an ad-hoc format and prefix."
- added `r.backend-config-fields` (MUST): "BackendConfig must carry the audit device's salt view, salt configuration and opaque user configuration so a backend can be constructed without reaching back into the server."
- added `r.backend-interface` (MUST): "An audit backend must be the Backend interface, exposing LogRequest(context.Context, *logical.LogInput) error, LogResponse(context.Context, *logical.LogInput) error, LogTestMessage(context.Context, *logical.LogInput, map[string]string) error, GetHash(context.Context, string) (string, error), Reload(context.Context) error and Invalidate(context.Context)."
- added `r.factory-type` (SHOULD): "Audit backends must be constructed through the Factory type alias rather than a concrete constructor, so each device package supplies its own factory value."
- added `r.format-tests` (SHOULD): "The formatting and hashing behaviour must stay covered by tests in format_test.go, format_json_test.go and hashstructure_test.go."
- added `r.formatter-interface` (MUST): "A formatter must implement Formatter by offering FormatRequest(context.Context, io.Writer, FormatterConfig, *logical.LogInput) error and FormatResponse(context.Context, io.Writer, FormatterConfig, *logical.LogInput) error, taking a FormatterConfig to carry per-mount formatting options."
- added `r.hash-helpers` (MUST): "HashString must HMAC a single string with the salt, and HashAuth, HashRequest, HashResponse and HashWrapInfo must return salted copies of *logical.Auth, *logical.Request, *logical.Response and *wrapping.ResponseWrapInfo with an error, honouring the HMACAccessor flag and, for requests and responses, the nonHMACDataKeys and elideListResponseData options."
- added `r.hash-structure-walk` (MUST): "HashStructure(data any, cb HashCallback, ignoredKeys []string, elideListResponseData bool) error must walk an arbitrary value with reflectwalk and invoke the HashCallback on each qualifying primitive, skipping the ignored keys, so nested maps, slices and structs are hashed in place."
- added `r.hash-walker-callbacks` (MUST): "The reflectwalk visitor used by HashStructure must be a hashWalker implementing Enter(reflectwalk.Location) error, Exit(reflectwalk.Location) error, Map(reflect.Value) error, MapElem(m, k, v reflect.Value) error, Slice(reflect.Value) error, SliceElem(i int, elem reflect.Value) error and Primitive(reflect.Value) error, so the callback sees map keys as well as values and can elide list response data."
- added `r.json-format-writer` (MUST): "JSONFormatWriter must implement AuditFormatWriter, with WriteRequest and WriteResponse emitting the entry as JSON to the writer and Salt returning the active salt from the context."

### third-party-openbao-internal-builtin-audit-file

- intent: "" -> "This context exists so that the file audit device can be reasoned about and changed without reading the whole vendored OpenBao tree. It records the contract Factory must honor when it turns operator configuration into a running backend, the file-mode and format validation rules that guard audit log creation, and the audit.Backend methods Backend exposes. The companion test file pins the observable behavior of the file-mode handling, so the spec must describe that validation as it is actually implemented rather than as a cleaner design."
- added `r.backend-satisfies-audit-interface` (MUST): "Backend must satisfy the audit.Backend interface by providing Salt, GetHash, LogRequest, LogResponse, LogTestMessage, Reload and Invalidate."
- added `r.bool-options-parsed` (MUST): "Factory parses hmac_accessor (default true), log_raw (default false) and elide_list_responses (default false) with strconv.ParseBool and returns the parse error on failure."
- added `r.eager-open-sanity-check` (MUST): "Factory opens the target file during construction, except when the path is stdout or discard, and wraps the failure as "sanity check failed; unable to open %q for writing: %w"."
- added `r.factory-requires-salt` (MUST): "Factory returns an error "nil salt config" when conf.SaltConfig is nil and "nil salt view" when conf.SaltView is nil."
- added `r.format-json-only` (MUST): "Factory defaults format to "json", rejects "jsonx" with the removed-formatting error, and rejects any other value with "unknown format type %q"."
- added `r.formatter-writer-wiring` (MUST): "Factory installs an audit.JSONFormatWriter on b.formatter with Prefix taken from conf.Config["prefix"] and SaltFunc set to b.Salt."
- added `r.get-hash` (MUST): "Backend.GetHash returns the HMAC hash of the given data string using the loaded salt, or an error when no salt is available."
- added `r.log-request-response` (MUST): "Backend.LogRequest formats the incoming logical.LogInput and writes it to the configured path, and Backend.LogResponse does the same for responses, both returning formatting or write errors."
- added `r.log-test-message` (MUST): "Backend.LogTestMessage takes an extra config map so an audit device can be verified without persisting a real audit entry."
- added `r.mode-handling` (MUST): "Factory defaults the file mode to 0o600; mode 0o000 stat-ings the path (unless it is stdout or discard) and leaves the existing file mode untouched; any other value must be a regular file mode and has its executable bits cleared with mode &^= 0o111 as mitigation for CVE-2025-6000."
- added `r.path-from-config` (MUST): "Factory resolves the output path from conf.Config["file_path"], falling back to conf.Config["path"], and errors with "file_path is required" when neither key is present."
- added `r.reload-reopen` (MUST): "Backend.Reload takes a context and re-opens the log file, and Backend.Invalidate takes a context and drops the open handle so a deleted file is recreated on the next write."
- added `r.salt-available` (MUST): "Backend.Salt returns the cached salt.Salt, loading it via salt.NewSalt(ctx, b.saltView, b.saltConfig) under a mutex on first use, and caches nil plus the error when loading fails."
- added `r.stdout-discard-normalized` (MUST): "Factory normalizes the path case-insensitively so that "stdout" and "discard" become the lowercase sentinels used by the rest of the backend."
- added `r.tests-cover-file-mode` (SHOULD): "The test file should keep covering new-file mode, existing-file mode, mode 0000, executable mode rejection and irregular mode rejection, plus the request benchmark."

### third-party-openbao-internal-builtin-audit-http

- intent: "" -> "This context exists so that the HTTP audit device can be described, tested and reimplemented without reading the vendored source: it fixes the contract the audit subsystem depends on (a Backend that hashes with a salt, encodes log input through a JSON formatter, and POSTs the entry to a configured URI), the exact configuration keys and defaults Factory honours, and the failure modes callers must see at construction time rather than at first log. It also records the test-only handler the package uses to stand in for a remote audit endpoint, so end-to-end behaviour of the HTTP path is observable from tests."
- added `r.backend-implements-audit-contract` (MUST): "Backend supplies Salt, GetHash, LogRequest, LogResponse, LogTestMessage, Reload and Invalidate so that it satisfies the audit.Backend interface."
- added `r.factory-rejects-nil-salt-config` (MUST): "Factory returns an error when conf.SaltConfig is nil."
- added `r.factory-rejects-nil-salt-view` (MUST): "Factory returns an error when conf.SaltView is nil."
- added `r.format-config-defaults` (MUST): "Factory sets hmacAccessor true by default, logRaw false by default, and elideListResponses false by default, parsing each config value as a bool when present and failing on a parse error."
- added `r.format-json-only` (MUST): "Factory defaults the format to json, accepts only json, rejects jsonx with an error stating that jsonx formatting has been removed, and rejects any other format value."
- added `r.formatter-writer-wired` (MUST): "Factory assigns the Backend formatter an audit.JSONFormatWriter carrying the prefix config value and Backend.Salt as its SaltFunc."
- added `r.headers-json-decoded-and-expanded` (MUST): "When the headers config key is present, Factory unmarshals it as a JSON map of string to string slice and runs parseutil.ParsePath with env expansion on every header value, adding each expanded value to the http.Header."
- added `r.http-client-checked-at-factory` (MUST): "Factory calls the backend getClient helper and fails when client construction returns an error, so a bad HTTP client setup is caught at audit device creation."
- added `r.integration-test-exercises-factory` (SHOULD): "The package test suite drives Factory against the test audit handler so that the HTTP audit path is exercised end to end."
- added `r.log-entry-encoded-and-posted` (MUST): "LogRequest, LogResponse and LogTestMessage encode the logical.LogInput through the configured formatter and deliver the buffered entry to the configured uri with the configured headers."
- added `r.reload-and-invalidate` (MUST): "Backend.Reload accepts a context and returns an error, and Backend.Invalidate accepts a context and returns nothing, matching the audit.Backend interface used by the reload and cache invalidation paths."
- added `r.salt-backed-by-salt-view` (MUST): "Backend.Salt returns the salt.Salt for the backend, using the salt view and salt config captured by Factory, and Backend.GetHash hashes data with that salt."
- added `r.test-handler-records-logs` (SHOULD): "GetTestAuditHandler returns an http.HandlerFunc that appends each decoded audit entry to the caller-supplied logs slice under the caller-supplied mutex, verifies the required headers, and increments the caller-supplied bad request counter for malformed input."
- added `r.uri-config-required` (MUST): "Factory requires the uri config key and fails when it is absent."
- added `r.uri-resolved-and-parsed` (MUST): "Factory resolves the uri with parseutil.ParsePath using WithNoTrimSpaces and WithErrorOnMissingEnv, then validates it with url.Parse, and fails on either error."

### third-party-openbao-internal-builtin-audit-socket

- intent: "" -> "The context exists so the socket audit device has a specification anchored to its real Go symbols: one exported factory, one exported Backend type, and the eight methods that make the type usable as an audit.Backend. It names the entry points a caller or a sibling audit device (file, http, syslog) would rely on, and records the signatures those callers can depend on without reading the file."
- added `r.backend-implements-audit-interface` (MUST): "Backend must satisfy the audit.Backend interface by providing LogRequest, LogResponse, LogTestMessage, GetHash, Reload, Salt and Invalidate, so it can be registered as an audit device next to the file, http and syslog backends."
- added `r.factory-constructs-backend` (MUST): "Factory takes a context and an *audit.BackendConfig and returns an audit.Backend together with an error, constructing the socket Backend from the supplied configuration and returning an error rather than a partially usable backend when construction fails."
- added `r.get-hash` (MUST): "GetHash takes a context and a data string, resolves the backend salt and returns the salted hash of the data as a string with an error, so sensitive values are logged hashed."
- added `r.invalidate-releases` (MUST): "Invalidate takes a context and returns nothing, releasing the socket connection and the resources the backend holds so a shut-down backend leaves nothing open."
- added `r.log-request` (MUST): "LogRequest takes a context and a *logical.LogInput, formats the request audit entry and writes it to the socket, returning an error when the entry cannot be formatted or delivered."
- added `r.log-response` (MUST): "LogResponse takes a context and a *logical.LogInput, formats the response audit entry and writes it to the socket, returning an error when the entry cannot be formatted or delivered."
- added `r.log-test-message` (MUST): "LogTestMessage takes a context, a *logical.LogInput and a map of configuration overrides, and writes a test audit entry to the socket, reporting an error when the test entry cannot be emitted."
- added `r.reload-reconnects` (SHOULD): "Reload takes a context and returns an error, re-establishing the socket connection so a backend whose peer went away resumes logging without a restart."
- added `r.salt-accessor` (MUST): "Salt takes a context and returns the backend's *salt.Salt with an error, providing the salt that GetHash and the audit formatter hash accessor and sensitive values with."

### third-party-openbao-internal-builtin-audit-syslog

- intent: "" -> "This context exists to pin down the contract of the syslog audit device so that the vendored OpenBao audit subsystem can construct it and route audit entries through it without reading the implementation. It records that syslog plugs into the same Factory/Backend interface that the audit package declares and that the file, http and socket packages also satisfy, which lets the registry treat every sink uniformly and lets a change to one backend be checked against the shared contract."
- added `r.backend-type` (MUST): "The syslog audit device state must be held in the Backend struct declared in the syslog package."

- added `r.log-request` (MUST): "Backend must implement LogRequest to write a request audit entry from the given *logical.LogInput."
- added `r.log-response` (MUST): "Backend must implement LogResponse to write a response audit entry from the given *logical.LogInput."
- added `r.log-test-message` (MUST): "Backend must implement LogTestMessage so that an operator-triggered test entry is written using the supplied *logical.LogInput and the per-call config map."
- added `r.no-context-reload-invalidate` (SHOULD): "Reload and Invalidate should not depend on the passed context, taking it unnamed, because neither needs cancellation while re-reading or clearing state."
- added `r.reload` (MUST): "Backend must implement Reload to re-read the device configuration and return an error when the reload fails."
- added `r.salt` (MUST): "Backend must implement Salt to return the *salt.Salt used when formatting audit entries, or an error."

### third-party-openbao-internal-builtin-credential-approle

- intent: "" -> "This context documents the vendored OpenBao AppRole credential backend that lives in the deno-kcp tree, so the plugin factory surface, the role/login/tidy paths, the salt lifecycle and the SecretID storage model stay described as they actually are. It exists to anchor the backend's exported entry points and its behavioural obligations to concrete code references before any change is made to third_party/openbao."
- added `r.backend-construction` (MUST): "Backend must allocate lock sets for roles, RoleIDs, SecretIDs and SecretID accessors, and must attach a framework.Backend of type credential that registers rolePaths, pathLogin and pathTidySecretID, sets AuthRenew to pathLoginRenew, PeriodicFunc to periodicFunc, InitializeFunc to Initialize, exposes login as unauthenticated and marks the SecretID and SecretID accessor prefixes as local storage."

- added `r.initialize-salt` (MUST): "Initialize must return without creating a salt when the replication state is DR secondary or performance standby, or when the mount is not local and the state is performance secondary; otherwise it must create the initial salt via Salt and wrap any failure as "error creating initial salt"."
- added `r.login-path` (MUST): "The login path must authenticate a RoleID and SecretID pair and issue a token, and must supply the auth renew handler."
- added `r.role-paths` (MUST): "The role paths must create, read, list, delete and configure AppRole roles, including their RoleID and SecretID material."
- added `r.salt-provisioning` (MUST): "backend.Salt must return the salt backed by the given logical storage, creating it on first use."
- added `r.secret-id-response` (MUST): "secretIDStorageEntry.ToResponseData must project a stored SecretID entry into a map[string]any suitable for an API response, reporting secret_id_accessor, secret_id_num_uses, secret_id_ttl in seconds, creation_time, expiration_time, last_updated_time, metadata, cidr_list and token_bound_cidrs, and substituting an empty string slice when TokenBoundCIDRs is empty."
- added `r.secret-id-validation` (MUST): "SecretID and RoleID validation must reject entries that are expired or bound to a different role."
- added `r.test-coverage` (SHOULD): "The backend, login, role, tidy and validation behaviour should be covered by the package's Go tests."
- added `r.tidy-secret-id` (MUST): "The tidy secret ID path must remove expired and orphaned SecretID entries."

### third-party-openbao-internal-builtin-credential-approle-cmd-approle

- intent: "" -> "This context exists so the AppRole credential backend can run as an out-of-process OpenBao plugin binary. It isolates the harness boilerplate — flag parsing, TLS provider derivation, and multiplexed serving — from the backend implementation, which lives in the parent `approle` package and is reached only through the `approle.Factory` symbol. Keeping this file thin means the backend stays testable and buildable without the plugin harness, while the binary itself remains compileable against host versions that predate plugin AutoMTLS."
- added `r.legacy-automtls-compat` (SHOULD): "`TLSProviderFunc` remains set on the serve options to keep backwards compatibility with host versions that do not support plugin AutoMTLS, as noted in the source comment."
- added `r.no-owned-abstractions` (SHOULD): "The file stays a thin entrypoint: it declares no types and exports no interfaces, delegating backend behavior entirely to `approle.Factory`."
- added `r.package-main-entrypoint` (MUST): "The file declares `package main` and provides the process entrypoint `func main()` that starts the AppRole plugin binary."
- added `r.parse-plugin-flags` (MUST): "`main` constructs an `api.PluginAPIClientMeta`, takes its flag set, and parses `os.Args[1:]` through it, so the plugin honors the harness-supplied plugin API flags."
- added `r.serve-approle-factory` (MUST): "`main` calls `plugin.ServeMultiplex` with `plugin.ServeOpts` whose `BackendFactoryFunc` is `approle.Factory`, so the multiplexed plugin serves the AppRole credential backend."
- added `r.serve-error-exit` (MUST): "When `plugin.ServeMultiplex` returns an error, `main` builds an `hclog` logger, logs the message "plugin shutting down" with the error, and calls `os.Exit(1)`; on success it returns normally."
- added `r.tls-provider-from-meta` (MUST): "`main` obtains the TLS config via `apiClientMeta.GetTLSConfig()` and converts it into a provider function with `api.VaultPluginTLSProvider`, passing that function as `TLSProviderFunc` to the serve options."

### third-party-openbao-internal-builtin-credential-cert

- intent: "" -> "This context exists so the vendored certificate auth backend can be described and reasoned about as a unit inside deno-kcp without reading the whole OpenBao tree. It fixes the contract of the plugin boundary (Factory, Backend), the persisted models (CertEntry, CRLInfo, CDPInfo, RevokedSerialInfo, config), the login parsing type ParsedCert, the CLI surface CLIHandler, and the test-only OCSP responder abstractions (Source, Stats, Responder) so that callers and tests can rely on those shapes staying stable."
- added `r.backend-credential-type` (MUST): "Backend must declare itself a credential backend, leave login unauthenticated, and bind AuthRenew, Invalidate, InitializeFunc and PeriodicFunc."
- added `r.backend-registers-paths` (MUST): "Backend must build the framework backend with the config, login, cert list, cert, CRL list and CRL paths registered."
- added `r.cert-entry-model` (MUST): "CertEntry must be the persisted model for a trusted certificate, holding its display name, certificate, allowed names, and OCSP and CRL settings."
- added `r.cert-entry-read` (MUST): "backend.Cert must load a single certificate entry by name from logical.Storage and return a *CertEntry."
- added `r.cli-auth` (MUST): "CLIHandler.Auth must read the certificate and key material from the flag map and perform the login against the API client, prompting interactively unless nonInteractive is set."
- added `r.cli-help` (SHOULD): "CLIHandler.Help must return the usage text listing the certificate and key flags."
- added `r.config-read` (MUST): "backend.Config must read the stored backend configuration from logical.Storage and return a *config."
- added `r.crl-models` (SHOULD): "CRLInfo, CDPInfo and RevokedSerialInfo must model a fetched CRL, a CRL distribution point, and a revoked serial with its revocation time."
- added `r.crl-update-mutex` (MUST): "Backend must initialize the CRL update mutex before the backend is returned."
- added `r.factory-builds-backend` (MUST): "Factory must construct the certificate auth backend from a logical.BackendConfig and return it as a logical.Backend, or an error if Setup fails."
- added `r.in-memory-source` (MUST): "InMemorySource must be a Source usable in tests, answering each ocsp.Request with response bytes and headers."
- added `r.login-parsed-cert` (MUST): "ParsedCert must carry the parsed client certificate together with its extracted leaf and chain so login can match it against configuration."
- added `r.ocsp-source` (MUST): "Source must abstract an OCSP responder: Response takes an *ocsp.Request and returns the response bytes and HTTP headers, or an error."
- added `r.responder-construction` (MUST): "NewResponder must build a *Responder from a logger, a Source and a Stats sink."
- added `r.responder-logging` (MAY): "Responder may log through the logger it was built with, which must accept variadic arguments."
- added `r.responder-serve-http` (MUST): "Responder.ServeHTTP must decode the OCSP request from the HTTP request, obtain the response from its Source, record the status, and write the response to the client."
- added `r.responder-stats` (SHOULD): "Stats must expose the last observed OCSP response status so tests can assert on the responder's behavior."

### third-party-openbao-internal-builtin-credential-cert-cmd-cert

- intent: "" -> "This context exists to pin down the contract of the cert plugin's binary entry point: the sequence of flag parsing, TLS material derivation from the plugin API client meta, and the multiplexed serve call that registers `cert.Factory` as the backend factory. It matters because the entry point is the boundary between the plugin process and the OpenBao/Vault plugin protocol, and because the explicit `TLSProviderFunc` is what keeps the plugin loadable by older Vault versions without AutoMTLS. It also fixes the failure behavior — log and exit non-zero — so a failed serve is never silently ignored. The context deliberately holds no business logic: everything about certificate auth lives in the cert package, and this file must stay a thin bootstrapper."
- added `r.log-and-exit-on-serve-failure` (MUST): "When `plugin.ServeMultiplex` returns an error, the cert command's `main` MUST build a logger with `hclog.New(&hclog.LoggerOptions{})`, log the error under the message `plugin shutting down` with the `error` key, and terminate with `os.Exit(1)`."
- added `r.parse-plugin-api-client-flags` (MUST): "The cert command's `main` MUST construct an `api.PluginAPIClientMeta`, take its `FlagSet`, and parse `os.Args[1:]` before serving, and MUST derive the TLS config and the TLS provider function from that same meta."
- added `r.remain-thin-package-main-binary` (SHOULD): "The cert command SHOULD remain a `package main` binary whose only logic is flag parsing, TLS setup, and the serve call, leaving all backend behavior to the imported cert package."
- added `r.retain-tls-provider-for-automtls-backcompat` (MUST): "The cert command's `main` MUST set `TLSProviderFunc` on the serve options from `api.VaultPluginTLSProvider(tlsConfig)` so the plugin stays loadable by Vault versions that do not support plugin AutoMTLS."
- added `r.serve-cert-factory-as-multiplexed-plugin` (MUST): "The cert command's `main` MUST register the cert credential backend by passing `cert.Factory` as `BackendFactoryFunc` to `plugin.ServeMultiplex`."

### third-party-openbao-internal-builtin-credential-jwt

- intent: "" -> "This context exists because the JWT/OIDC auth plugin is vendored third-party OpenBao code inside deno-kcp, and it needs one spec that states what the package actually provides: the backend factory, the CLI login handler, the QR rendering writer, the CustomProvider contract, the three optional provider extension interfaces, the provider registry and resolution function, and the five concrete provider implementations. Recording these interfaces and requirements makes the vendored plugin's public surface explicit, so that changes to it, or reliance on it from elsewhere in the repository, can be checked against a stated contract instead of re-reading the files."
- added `r.azure-provider` (MUST): "AzureProvider must implement CustomProvider by providing Initialize and SensitiveKeys, and must implement GroupsFetcher to read Azure group claims using a token source."
- added `r.cel-role-response-data` (SHOULD): "celRoleEntry must expose ToResponseData so a CEL role can be returned to callers as a map including its name, program, message, leeway durations, and bound audiences."
- added `r.cli-handler-auth-and-help` (MUST): "CLIHandler must implement the login handler surface by providing Auth, which returns an api.Secret from a client and argument map, and Help, which returns the handler's usage string."
- added `r.custom-provider-contract` (MUST): "CustomProvider must declare Initialize, which configures the provider from a jwtConfig, and SensitiveKeys, which lists config keys that must be treated as sensitive."
- added `r.factory-builds-backend` (MUST): "Factory must construct the JWT auth backend via backend() and call Setup with the given context and logical.BackendConfig, returning the error when setup fails."
- added `r.groups-fetcher-extension` (MAY): "A provider may implement GroupsFetcher to resolve group membership for the supplied backend, claims, role, and token source."
- added `r.gsuite-provider` (MUST): "GSuiteProvider must implement CustomProvider and both the GroupsFetcher and UserInfoFetcher extensions, using GSuiteProviderConfig for its credentials."
- added `r.ibmisam-provider` (MUST): "IBMISAMProvider must implement CustomProvider with a no-op Initialize, SensitiveKeys, and a GroupsFetcher that reads IBM ISAM group claims."
- added `r.keyset-discovery-extension` (MAY): "A provider may implement KeySetDiscovery to supply its own jwt.KeySet for token verification instead of static keys."
- added `r.kubernetes-provider` (MUST): "KubernetesProvider must implement CustomProvider plus KeySetDiscovery, initializing from jwtConfig and fetching the cluster key set over HTTP with bearer authentication."
- added `r.new-provider-config-resolves` (MUST): "NewProviderConfig must select and initialize a provider for the given jwtConfig from the supplied provider map, returning an error when the configured type is unknown or initialization fails."
- added `r.provider-map-registry` (MUST): "ProviderMap must return the builtin provider registry keyed by provider type name, mapping each name to its CustomProvider implementation."
- added `r.qr-writer-renders-matrix` (SHOULD): "qrWriter must write a qrcode.Matrix to its io.Writer as block characters, using truecolor escapes when COLORTERM is truecolor or 24bit, and Close must report no error."
- added `r.secureauth-provider` (MUST): "SecureAuthProvider must implement CustomProvider with a no-op Initialize, SensitiveKeys, and a GroupsFetcher that reads SecureAuth group claims."
- added `r.tls-overrides` (SHOULD): "jwtAuthBackend must allow a config path to override the TLS client configuration by appending root CAs from PEM and by constraining the set of allowed server names."
- added `r.user-info-fetcher-extension` (MAY): "A provider may implement UserInfoFetcher to enrich allClaims from the provider's userinfo endpoint for the supplied backend and role."

### third-party-openbao-internal-builtin-credential-jwt-cmd-jwt

- intent: "" -> "This context exists to capture the process-level bootstrap that turns the JWT/OIDC credential backend into a runnable OpenBao/Vault plugin binary. It is deliberately thin: it owns flag parsing, TLS config derivation, and the `plugin.ServeMultiplex` wiring, while all backend behavior lives in the jwtauth package imported as `jwtauth`. It must stay correct because it is the only path by which the JWT backend is mounted as an external plugin, and the explicit `TLSProviderFunc` exists purely to keep older Vault versions without AutoMTLS working."
- added `r.exit-nonzero-on-error` (MUST): "A failure from flag parsing or from `plugin.ServeMultiplex` MUST be reported with `log.Println` and MUST terminate the process with `os.Exit(1)`."
- added `r.flag-parse-from-args` (MUST): "The entry point MUST construct an `api.PluginAPIClientMeta`, take its `FlagSet()`, and parse `os.Args[1:]` through that flag set."
- added `r.no-exported-api` (SHOULD): "The package SHOULD remain a `main` package that exposes only the executable entry point, exporting no identifiers for other packages to import."
- added `r.serve-jwt-factory-multiplex` (MUST): "The entry point MUST serve the JWT credential backend through `plugin.ServeMultiplex` with `BackendFactoryFunc` set to `jwtauth.Factory`, the factory of `github.com/openbao/openbao/v2/internal/builtin/credential/jwt`."
- added `r.tls-provider-for-backcompat` (MUST): "The entry point MUST set `TLSProviderFunc` on the serve options to `api.VaultPluginTLSProvider` of the config returned by `apiClientMeta.GetTLSConfig()`, so the plugin keeps backwards compatibility with Vault versions that do not support plugin AutoMTLS."

### third-party-openbao-internal-builtin-credential-kubernetes

- intent: "" -> "This context exists to specify the vendored OpenBao Kubernetes credential backend as it stands in third_party: how the credential backend is constructed and registered, how its config, login and role paths are served, how service account JWTs are reviewed against the Kubernetes TokenReview API, how the local service account token and CA certificate are cached between re-reads, how role namespace constraints are validated, and how the OpenBao CLI authenticates with this method. It fixes the package's exported and receiver-side interfaces and the invariants the construction, caching, token review and CLI paths must keep, so downstream work in deno-kcp can rely on the vendored behaviour instead of re-deriving it from source."
- added `r.backend-defaults` (MUST): "Backend must initialize the backend with caching readers for the local service account JWT and the local CA certificate, a default HTTP client, a default TLS config, tokenReviewAPIFactory as the review factory, and newNsValidatorWrapper as the namespace validator factory."
- added `r.backend-wiring` (MUST): "Backend must return a *kubeAuthBackend whose embedded framework.Backend has BackendType logical.TypeCredential, registers configPath and login as unauthenticated-capable paths together with the role paths, seals configPath in storage, and sets AuthRenew, InitializeFunc and Clean to the backend's own handlers."
- added `r.caching-file-read-cached-path` (MUST): "cachingFileReader.ReadFile must return the cached buffer without touching disk when the current time is still before the cached entry's expiry, taking only a read lock on that fast path."
- added `r.caching-file-read-refresh` (MUST): "cachingFileReader.ReadFile must, when the cache is stale, take the write lock, read the file at its configured path, store the contents with an expiry of now plus the reader's ttl, and return them, propagating any read error to the caller."
- added `r.cli-auth-method` (MUST): "CLIHandler must implement the API client's auth method contract with Auth, which takes the client, the method's config map and the nonInteractive flag and returns an *api.Secret, and Help, which returns the method's usage string."
- added `r.dont-verify-signature` (MUST): "The backend must provide a DontVerifySignature type whose VerifySignature method accepts a context and a token and returns the token's claims as a map[string]any without verifying the signature, so deployments that delegate validation to the Kubernetes API can skip local verification."
- added `r.factory-builds-backend` (MUST): "The package must expose Factory, taking a context and a *logical.BackendConfig, that constructs the Kubernetes backend with Backend and calls Setup on it before returning it as a logical.Backend, so the framework can register it as a credential backend."
- added `r.namespace-validation` (SHOULD): "Role namespace constraints should be checked by the namespace validator wrapper, which rejects patterns that do not match at least one namespace, so a role cannot be created that no service account could ever satisfy."
- added `r.paths-config-login-role` (MUST): "The backend must serve the config path for cluster connection settings and token reviewer credentials, the login path for service account JWT login, and the role paths for creating, reading, listing and deleting Kubernetes roles with their bound service accounts, namespaces and audiences."
- added `r.test-coverage` (SHOULD): "The backend, caching file reader, config path, login path and role path behaviour should be covered by table-driven Go tests that reuse the shared helpers in helpers.go and common_test.go."
- added `r.token-review-indirection` (MUST): "Token review must go through the tokenReviewer interface, with tokenReviewAPI as the production implementation that calls the Kubernetes TokenReview API with a context, HTTP client, JWT and audiences, and mockTokenReview as the test implementation used in place of it."

### third-party-openbao-internal-builtin-credential-kubernetes-cmd-kubernetes

- intent: "" -> "This context exists to pin down the contract of the Kubernetes credential backend's plugin binary: which SDK entry point it serves through, how it obtains its TLS provider, and how it fails. It gives reviewers and downstream tooling a stable statement of the entry point's obligations, because the file itself is a few statements of wiring whose correctness is entirely about calling the OpenBao plugin SDK in the right order with the right arguments."
- added `r.fatal-exit` (MUST): "A failure from flag parsing or from ServeMultiplex must be logged through the hclog logger at error level with the message 'plugin shutting down' and the error attached under the 'error' key, then the process must exit with status code 1."
- added `r.flag-parsing` (MUST): "The process must parse its API client plugin flags from os.Args[1:] with the flag set returned by api.PluginAPIClientMeta.FlagSet, and must treat a parse error as fatal."
- added `r.plugin-serve-multiplex` (MUST): "The entry point must serve the Kubernetes credential backend through plugin.ServeMultiplex using a plugin.ServeOpts whose BackendFactoryFunc is kubeauth.Factory."
- added `r.tls-provider-compat` (MUST): "ServeMultiplex must receive a TLSProviderFunc built by api.VaultPluginTLSProvider over the config from api.PluginAPIClientMeta.GetTLSConfig, so the plugin keeps backwards compatibility with Vault versions that do not support plugin AutoMTLS."

### third-party-openbao-internal-builtin-credential-kubernetes-integrationtest

- intent: "" -> "This context exists to verify, end to end against a real Kubernetes cluster, that the OpenBao Kubernetes credential backend authenticates projected service-account JWTs correctly and rejects the cases it should. It is an opt-in integration harness rather than library code, requiring INTEGRATION_TESTS to be set plus a cluster with a test namespace, a deployed Vault/OpenBao reachable via port forward, and a test-token-reviewer-account service account with TokenReview access. Its reason to exist is to exercise the login path and the boundary behaviors — token reviewer configuration, namespace label selectors, unauthorized service accounts, and audience binding — that unit tests cannot reproduce without a live API server."
- added `r.audience-validation-matrix` (MUST): "Audience validation must be covered by a table-driven test pairing configured audience values (default, "a", unset) with tokens minted for default, "a", and "b" audiences, asserting success or a 403 error for each combination."
- added `r.forbidden-error-shape` (MUST): "Rejected logins must surface as an *api.ResponseError with StatusCode 403, tested for a bad token reviewer JWT, an unauthorized service account, a mismatching namespace selector, and non-matching audiences."
- added `r.gated-by-env-var` (MUST): "The integration test package must run its tests only when the INTEGRATION_TESTS environment variable is non-empty; otherwise TestMain must return without invoking m.Run."
- added `r.kubernetes-dev-mount-setup` (MUST): "setupKubernetesAuth must enable the kubernetes-dev auth method at sys/auth/kubernetes, write auth/kubernetes/config and auth/kubernetes/role/test-role, and return a cleanup that deletes the mount."
- added `r.namespace-label-selector` (MUST): "A role using bound_service_account_namespace_selector must permit login when the selector labels match the namespace and must reject login with HTTP 403 when they do not."
- added `r.override-configuration` (SHOULD): "setupKubernetesAuth should accept optional mount and role configuration overrides that replace the default kubernetes_host and bound service account name/namespace settings when non-empty."
- added `r.port-forward-to-api` (MUST): "Before running tests, the harness must set up Kubernetes port forwarding to the vault-0 pod in the test namespace and export BAO_ADDR pointing at the resulting local port with BAO_TOKEN set to root."
- added `r.successful-login` (MUST): "A login to auth/kubernetes/login with role test-role and a token for a bound service account must succeed, both with the default mount configuration and with an explicit token_reviewer_jwt."
- added `r.token-minting` (MUST): "Test tokens must be minted through the Kubernetes TokenRequest API for a named service account in the test namespace, returning the token from the response status."

### third-party-openbao-internal-builtin-credential-kubernetes-integrationtest-k8s

- intent: "" -> "This context exists to give integration tests of the Kubernetes auth backend a way to talk to a Vault/OpenBao instance that runs inside a Kubernetes pod. Because the container is not reachable directly from the test host, the package provides the two primitives the tests need: an authenticated clientset built from a caller-named kubeconfig context, and a port-forward that exposes the pod's Vault port 8200 on a free local port, together with a close function so the tunnel can be torn down. Both helpers share the same kubeconfig resolution path, and every failure is returned as a wrapped error naming the step that failed, so a broken test setup reports where it broke."
- added `r.client-from-kube-context` (MUST): "ClientFromKubeConfig must get its REST config from kubeConfig(kubeContext) and return a *kubernetes.Clientset built by kubernetes.NewForConfig, returning nil and the config error unwrapped if config loading fails, and nil with an error wrapping the cause as "failed to create client" if client construction fails."
- added `r.kube-context-selection` (MUST): "Config resolution must select the kubeconfig context named by kubeContext, applied as CurrentContext on clientcmd.ConfigOverrides over clientcmd.NewDefaultClientConfigLoadingRules via clientcmd.NewNonInteractiveDeferredLoadingClientConfig, and a failure must surface as an error wrapping the cause as "failed to setup config"."
- added `r.port-forward-config-and-client` (MUST): "SetupPortForwarding must resolve its config through kubeConfig(kubeContext) and build its clientset with kubernetes.NewForConfig, returning local port 0, a nil close function and the config error unwrapped on config failure, and wrapping client construction failure as "failed to create client"."
- added `r.port-forward-local-port-and-close` (MUST): "On readiness SetupPortForwarding must read the assigned port from forwarder.GetPorts, returning 0, nil and an error wrapping the cause as "failed to get forwarded ports" on failure, and on success return ports[0].Local as the local port together with a close function that sends on the stop channel and then calls forwarder.Close."
- added `r.port-forward-random-local-port` (MUST): "SetupPortForwarding must forward from a random free local port to port 8200 in the target pod, passing the forwarding spec "0:8200" to portforward.New with a fresh stop channel, a fresh ready channel, io.Discard for output and os.Stderr for errors, and must return 0, nil and the error unwrapped if portforward.New fails."
- added `r.port-forward-ready-or-error` (MUST): "SetupPortForwarding must run forwarder.ForwardPorts in a goroutine that reports its error on a channel, and must select between that error channel and the ready channel; an error arriving before readiness must return local port 0, a nil close function and an error wrapping the cause as "failed to start forwarding"."
- added `r.port-forward-spdy-dialer` (MUST): "SetupPortForwarding must build the dialer over the pod's portforward subresource URL (RESTClient POST on Resource "pods", the given namespace and pod name, SubResource "portforward") using spdy.RoundTripperFor(config) and spdy.NewDialer with method POST on an http.Client carrying that transport, returning 0, nil and an error wrapping the cause as "failed to create transport" if the round tripper cannot be made."

### third-party-openbao-internal-builtin-credential-kubernetes-integrationtest-vault

- intent: "" -> "This context exists to hold the Kubernetes RBAC fixture manifests that the openbao kubernetes credential backend integration test applies before running. The test needs a ServiceAccount that the Vault server can use to review other pods' tokens, and it needs namespace-listing permission for both that reviewer account and the vault account so the test scenarios can enumerate namespaces during the auth flow. Keeping these as standalone YAML files under integrationtest/vault lets the test harness apply them verbatim to a throwaway cluster, isolating the test from any pre-existing RBAC state."

- added `r.namespace-controller-binding-reviewer` (MUST): "Bind the test-token-reviewer-account ServiceAccount in namespace test to ClusterRole system:controller:namespace-controller via a ClusterRoleBinding named test-namespacelister-account-binding."

### third-party-openbao-internal-builtin-credential-token

- intent: "" -> "This context exists to pin down the token auth method's CLI surface: the exact handler type, the exact Auth signature the login command calls, and the exact help text and configuration keys the token method advertises. It is one of five sibling credential handler contexts, so recording the shared two-method contract here keeps the token variant distinguishable from cert, jwt, kubernetes and userpass variants that export identically named types and methods. Requirements are anchored to the observed declarations so the handler cannot drift from the login command's dynamic interface expectations or from its own documented flags."
- added `r.auth-signature` (MUST): "CLIHandler.Auth accepts the API client, the string-keyed configuration map, and a nonInteractive flag, and returns an API secret or an error, so the login command can dispatch to it dynamically."
