- added `r.transit-encrypt-decrypt-exercise` (MUST): "ExerciseTransitEncryptDecrypt exercises encrypt and decrypt round trips against the given mount and key name, taking the client, mount name and key name as its inputs."
- added `r.transit-key-requires-grant-before-use` (MUST): "ExerciseTransitForKey writes the transit key at transit/keys/<baseName> with type "external-key" and external_key_ref "kms:<baseName>" and requires that this write fails while no grant exists; it then creates the grant by writing sys/external-keys/configs/kms/keys/<baseName>/grants/transit, requires that write to succeed, and retries the same transit key write requiring success this time."
- added `r.transit-key-runs-capability-subtests` (MUST): "ExerciseTransitForKey runs an "encrypt-decrypt" subtest only when the encryptDecrypt flag is set and a "sign-verify" subtest only when the signVerify flag is set; each subtest runs in parallel and invokes the corresponding exercise twice, once against the "keys" mount and once against the "transit" mount, with the base name as the key name."
- added `r.transit-kms-entry-runs-both-suites` (MUST): "ExerciseTransitKMS runs two subtests named "transit" and "pki" against the supplied API client, delegating to ExerciseTransitWithTransitKMS and ExercisePKIWithTransitKMS respectively, so a single call covers both the transit-engine and PKI-engine external key flows."
- added `r.transit-sign-verify-exercise` (MUST): "ExerciseTransitSignVerify exercises sign and verify round trips against the given mount and key name, taking the client, mount name and key name as its inputs."
- added `r.transit-with-transit-kms-per-key-type` (MUST): "ExerciseTransitWithTransitKMS first calls SetupTransit, then for every key type in knownTransitKeyTypes runs a subtest named after the type: it writes a backing key at keys/keys/transit-<type> with the type, writes an external key config at sys/external-keys/configs/kms/keys/transit-<type> with name and version 1, and then calls ExerciseTransitForKey with the base name and the type's EncryptDecrypt and SignVerify capabilities."

### third-party-openbao-internal-vault-external-tests-kv

- intent: "" -> "This context exists to specify the black-box acceptance tests that guard the KVv2 secret engine's PATCH, subkeys and upgrade-handling behaviour. The tests are deliberately end-to-end: they build a cluster from a CoreConfig that registers logicalKv.Factory or logicalKv.VersionedKVFactory as the "kv" logical backend, mount kv-v2 over the sys API, and then assert on raw HTTP status codes and parsed secret bodies. The package pins three externally visible contracts, namely that PATCH requires a merge-patch content type and produces exactly one audit request and response record, that the subkeys endpoint reports nil subkeys with deletion or destruction metadata instead of leaking data, and that reopening a KVv2 mount whose policy and archive views were wiped does not emit a "cannot write to storage during setup" error. The retry helper exists because a freshly mounted KVv2 backend may still be performing its non-versioned-to-versioned upgrade when the first request arrives, so the tests must tolerate that transient failure rather than reporting it."
- added `r.kv-patch-audit-record-count` (MUST): "When the file audit backend records a write to kv/data/foo followed by a JSONMergePatch to the same path, decoding the audit log must yield exactly one record of type "request" and exactly one of type "response" whose request operation is "patch"."
- added `r.kv-patch-requires-merge-patch-content-type` (MUST): "A raw PATCH request to /v1/kv/data/foo sent with Content-Type "application/json" must be rejected with HTTP 415 Unsupported Media Type, so that only a merge-patch media type is accepted by the KVv2 data endpoint."
- added `r.kv-patch-root-token-merge-semantics` (MUST): "A JSONMergePatch issued with the cluster root token after writing {bar: baz, foo: qux} must set bar to "quux" and remove the foo key entirely, so a following read of kv/data/foo returns bar="quux" and a data map with no foo entry; a null value in the patch body deletes the key."
- added `r.kv-request-retry-absorbs-upgrade` (MUST): "kvRequestWithRetry must poll the supplied request closure once per second for at most twenty seconds and return as soon as the closure succeeds, tolerating repeated failures whose *api.ResponseError message contains "Upgrading from non-versioned to versioned data"; it must return the response and error unchanged for any other error, and must report "timeout expired waiting for upgrade" when the deadline is reached."
- added `r.kv-subkeys-current-version-tree` (MUST): "When multiple versions exist, a read of kv/subkeys/foo must succeed with HTTP 200 and the parsed subkeys value must deep-equal the nested key tree {foo: nil, bar: {a: {c: nil}, b: nil}, baz: nil}, so the endpoint returns only key structure of the current version and never the values."
- added `r.kv-subkeys-deleted-metadata` (MUST): "After a secret is deleted, a read of kv/subkeys/foo must return HTTP 404 and a parsed body whose subkeys value is nil and whose metadata map carries a non-empty string deletion_time."
- added `r.kv-subkeys-destroyed-metadata` (MUST): "After a secret version is destroyed, a read of kv/subkeys/foo must return HTTP 404 and a parsed body containing a subkeys key that is nil together with metadata whose destroyed flag is the boolean true."
- added `r.kv-subkeys-missing-path-not-found` (MUST): "A read of kv/subkeys/foo for a path that was never written must fail with HTTP 404 Not Found."
- added `r.kv-tests-use-real-cluster` (MUST): "Each test in the package must construct its backend through vault.NewTestCluster with a CoreConfig that registers the kv logical factory (logicalKv.VersionedKVFactory or logicalKv.Factory) and vaulthttp.Handler as the handler, start the cluster, wait for the core to become active with vault.TestWaitActive, and mount the versioned KV engine under the path "kv" with type "kv-v2" before exercising any endpoint."
- added `r.kvv2-upgrade-path-clean-slate` (MUST): "For the upgrade regression, the test must mount kv-v2, seal the cores with cluster.EnsureCoresSealed, delete the policy/ and archive/ subtrees beneath the KVv2 base path using logical.ClearView over physical.NewView on core.UnderlyingRawStorage, then unseal with testhelpers.EnsureCoresUnsealed, wait ten seconds, and fail if the captured hclog output contains "cannot write to storage during setup"."

### third-party-openbao-internal-vault-external-tests-metrics

- intent: "" -> "The context exists to pin down the externally observable behaviour of OpenBao's core metrics endpoint as seen from outside the vault package: which mount-table gauges appear, what their labels and values are, how they move when a new mount is added, and that leader and unseal gauges follow a leadership change. It is a black-box acceptance layer that talks to a real two-core cluster over the HTTP API rather than to internal metric registries, so it guards the metric names, label names and endpoint shape that operators and monitoring depend on."
- added `r.gauge-condition-check` (SHOULD): "gaugeConditionCheck returns an error equality gauge check for comparison failed only when the comparator is the string eq and the two integers differ; any other comparator value passes without error."
- added `r.gauge-search-helper-labels` (MUST): "gaugeSearchHelper returns the collected core.mount_table.size value on success; it selects only gauges whose local label is the string false and whose type label is the string logical, requires the core.mount_table.num_entries gauge to be seen and otherwise returns the sentinel max-int value together with the error No metrics reported for mount sizes, and returns the same sentinel together with an error when the entry gauge value fails the eq check against the expected value."
- added `r.kv-mount-increments-entry-gauge` (MUST): "After mounting a kv version 2 backend at path kv with version option 2, the same nonlocal logical core.mount_table.num_entries gauge equals 4 and core.mount_table.size stays non-zero; the test documents that on a transactional storage backend the size gauge reports only the new table entry, not a running total."
- added `r.leader-reelection-metrics-endpoint` (MUST): "TestLeaderReElectionMetrics requests GET /v1/sys/metrics with cluster.RootToken in the consts.AuthHeaderName header, reads and JSON-unmarshals the body into testhelpers.SysMetricsJSON, and errors when either the core.active or the core.unsealed gauge is absent or does not equal 1."
- added `r.leader-stepdown-metrics-follow` (MUST): "After calling client.Sys().StepDown on the active core, the test waits for core 1 to report active and repeats the same GET /v1/sys/metrics assertions through the core 1 client, so the core.active and core.unsealed gauges must both be present and equal 1 on the new leader."
- added `r.mount-table-nonlocal-logical-gauges` (MUST): "Before any user mount is added, the test asserts that the core.mount_table.num_entries gauge carrying labels local=false and type=logical equals 3, covering the cubbyhole, identity and kv mounts, and that the matching core.mount_table.size gauge is non-zero; a size of zero or less is a fatal failure."
- added `r.mount-table-test-cluster-shape` (MUST): "TestMountTableMetrics starts a two-core test cluster named mycluster with corehelpers.NewMockBuiltinRegistry as the builtin registry, vaulthttp.Handler as the handler, KeepStandbysSealed false, and a testhelpers.TestMetricSinkProvider sink on a one-minute interval, waits for core 0 to report active with vault.TestWaitActive before reading metrics, and defers cluster.Cleanup."

### third-party-openbao-internal-vault-external-tests-mfa

- intent: "" -> "The context exists to pin down the observable contract of the identity MFA API as exercised from outside the core: which provider types accept which config fields, that a method id is stable across re-writes of the same name, that a method read through the wrong type endpoint or a write to a non-existent method id fails, that global listing returns every method id and its key_info, that login enforcements require method ids plus at least one of auth_method_accessors, auth_method_types, identity_group_ids or identity_entity_ids, and that deleted entries stay deleted across seal and unseal. It is a black-box regression gate for the MFA subsystem, not production code."
- added `r.cluster-harness-per-test` (MUST): "Every test must build its cluster with vault.NewTestCluster using vaulthttp.Handler as the TestClusterOptions HandlerFunc, wait for the core to become active, clean the cluster on exit, and where a credential backend is needed register the userpass factory and enable auth at the userpass path before using its mount accessor."
- added `r.global-list-completeness` (MUST): "Listing identity/mfa/method globally must return a non-nil response whose keys entry and whose key_info map each contain exactly as many entries as the number of method configs created."
- added `r.global-method-read-and-delete` (MUST): "Reading identity/mfa/method/<method_id> without a provider type must return the method with its matching id, deleting an invalid path must fail, and after a successful delete on the id-bearing path a read must yield a nil response with a nil error (the 404 translation)."
- added `r.login-enforcement-crud` (MUST): "Writing a login enforcement to identity/mfa/login-enforcement/<name> must persist mfa_method_ids and auth_method_accessors such that a read returns equivalent slices, the name must appear in the list at identity/mfa/login-enforcement, a later write adding identity_group_ids and identity_entity_ids must be readable back as equivalent slices, and after delete the read must return nil response with nil error both immediately and after sealing and unsealing the cluster."
- added `r.login-enforcement-requires-method-ids` (MUST): "Writing an empty login enforcement config must fail with an error whose text contains "missing method ids"."
- added `r.login-enforcement-requires-one-scope` (MUST): "Writing a login enforcement with mfa_method_ids but none of auth_method_accessors, auth_method_types, identity_group_ids or identity_entity_ids must fail with an error whose text contains "One of auth_method_accessors, auth_method_types, identity_group_ids, identity_entity_ids must be specified"."
- added `r.method-crud-round-trip` (MUST): "For each of the totp, duo, okta and pingid providers, writing a config to identity/mfa/method/<type> must return a non-empty method_id; reading identity/mfa/method/<type>/<method_id> must return the same id with namespace_id "root" and an empty namespace_path; listing identity/mfa/method/<type> must include that method id in keys; an update through the same id-bearing path must be visible on the next read; and reading the id through a different provider type path must fail."
- added `r.method-name-uniqueness` (MUST): "Writing a method config that carries method_name must return a method_id, and re-writing the same method_name must return the same method_id; writing a second config with a new name must succeed; updating an existing method to take another method's name must fail; and a method_name that contains a slash such as "ns1/<original>" must be accepted."
- added `r.update-nonexistent-config-is-404` (MUST): "Writing a totp config to identity/mfa/method/totp/<id> for a method id that does not exist must fail with an error whose text contains "Code: 404"."

### third-party-openbao-internal-vault-external-tests-misc

- intent: "" -> "This context exists to specify the recovery-mode and panic-recovery external tests of the OpenBao `misc` test package, which exercise the server-level behavior of raw storage access under a recovery operation token and the ability of the cluster to seal cleanly after a logical backend panics. It pins the observable contract those tests assert: what a recovery-mode cluster must reject, what a recovery token must grant, what survives a seal/unseal round trip, and that a panicking backend must not deadlock core shutdown. It is a specification of existing test code, not of new code."
- added `r.noop-panic-mount-and-read` (MUST): "TestRecoverFromPanic must build a CoreConfig whose LogicalBackends map registers "noop" to backend.NoopBackendFactory and sets EnableRaw true, start a TestCluster with vaulthttp.Handler, mount a logical mount of type "noop" through core.Client.Sys().Mount, and then issue client.Logical().Read("noop/panic"), which must return a non-nil error."
- added `r.recovery-mode-token-gating` (MUST): "In recovery mode (CoreConfig.RecoveryMode true, TestClusterOptions.SkipInit true, handler properties RecoveryMode true and a RecoveryToken atomic.Value pointer), listing sys/raw/logical/<secretUUID> must fail with an error containing "403" both when the client token is "garbage" and when it is empty, and must still fail with "403" after a recovery operation token has been generated but before the client adopts it."
- added `r.recovery-raw-logical-mutation` (MUST): "With the generated recovery token set on the client, TestRecovery must successfully list sys/raw/logical/<secretUUID> and see keys equal to []any{"foo"}, and must successfully delete sys/raw/logical/<secretUUID>/foo through client.Logical().Delete."
- added `r.recovery-raw-namespace-entry` (MUST): "TestRecovery must list sys/raw/namespaces/<nsUUID> with the recovery token and require the returned data to contain a "keys" entry whose values include "core/"."
- added `r.recovery-root-generation-single-use` (MUST): "TestRecovery must generate a recovery operation token with testhelpers.GenerateRoot(t, cluster, testhelpers.GenerateRecovery) and must confirm that a second call through testhelpers.GenerateRootWithError with the same mode fails with the message "attempted to generate recovery operation token when already unsealed"."
- added `r.recovery-roundtrip-persistence` (MUST): "The final phase of TestRecovery must restart the cluster against the same inmem HA backend with recovery mode off, SkipInit true and the previously captured barrier keys, unseal with testhelpers.EnsureCoresUnsealed, wait for active, list secret/ using the original root token, and fail if the listing returns any data other than nil, proving the raw delete performed in recovery mode persisted."
- added `r.recovery-seed-state` (MUST): "TestRecovery must use a single inmem.NewInmemHA physical backend shared across all three phases, write map[string]any{"bar": 1.0} to secret/foo, assert that listing secret/ returns exactly the key "foo", capture the UUID of the secret/ mount and the UUID of a namespace created with Sys().CreateNamespace("ns1", nil), then seal the cores and save cluster.BarrierKeys for the later phases."
- added `r.recovery-token-cleared-between-phases` (SHOULD): "Each phase of TestRecovery should construct its own TestCluster with NumCores 1 and defer cluster.Cleanup, and should call cluster.EnsureCoresSealed before moving to the next phase, so the recovery and regular clusters never hold the storage backend open at the same time."
- added `r.seal-after-panic-no-deadlock` (MUST): "After the panicking read, TestRecoverFromPanic must wait for the core to become active with vault.TestWaitActive and then call cluster.EnsureCoresSealed(t), so a regression in panic recovery that prevents the core from sealing causes the test to deadlock rather than pass."

### third-party-openbao-internal-vault-external-tests-misc-misc-binary

- intent: "" -> "This context exists to pin down the behavior of the OpenBao recovery-mode external test so that the surrounding specification knows what that file guarantees: that recovery mode gates nearly every API path behind a recovery token, that sys/raw can be used under a recovery token to mutate persisted data directly, and that such mutations survive a return to normal mode. It is an acceptance test that only runs when a real OpenBao binary is supplied, so its requirements describe conditional, environment-gated behavior rather than production code paths."
- added `r.list-secrets-nil-safe` (SHOULD): "The listSecrets helper should return nil when the list response is nil, and otherwise decode the "keys" field with mapstructure into a []string so callers compare length only."
- added `r.parallel-test` (MAY): "The test may call t.Parallel() so it runs concurrently with other tests in the package."
- added `r.raw-delete-persists` (MUST): "After a final normal-mode restart, the test must require that listing secret/ returns zero keys, proving the raw deletion performed in recovery mode persisted across the restart."
- added `r.raw-delete-under-recovery` (MUST): "With the recovery token set, the test must list sys/raw/logical/<secretMountUUID> and require its keys to equal [foo], then delete sys/raw/logical/<secretMountUUID>/foo through the raw storage endpoint."
- added `r.recovery-mode-probe` (MUST): "The recovery-mode restart must stop the node, copy the original options, set Args to ["-recovery"], and start the node with a StartProbe that calls GenerateRecoveryOperationTokenStatusWithContext, because in recovery mode the only paths reachable without a recovery token are those used to generate one."
- added `r.recovery-token-single-use` (MUST): "In recovery mode the test must generate a recovery token with testcluster.GenerateRoot(cluster, testcluster.GenerateRecovery), must fail the test if a second GenerateRecovery call returns no error, and must then set the returned token on the client with SetToken."
- added `r.restart-preserves-secret` (MUST): "The restart helper must stop the first node, start it again with the original options, unseal all nodes, and wait for an active node; after the first restart the test must require that listing secret/ still returns at least one key."
- added `r.seed-secret-and-record-uuid` (MUST): "Before any restart, the test must mount a kv-v1 engine at secret/, write secret/foo with value {"bar": 1.0}, list secret/ and require the keys to equal [foo], then read the mount list and record the UUID of the secret/ mount for later raw access."
- added `r.single-node-trace-cluster` (MUST): "The test must start a Docker cluster with NumCores 1, image repo quay.io/openbao/openbao, tag latest, VaultBinary set to the BAO_BINARY value, node LogLevel TRACE, and must defer cluster cleanup."
- added `r.skip-without-binary` (MUST): "TestRecovery_Docker must read the BAO_BINARY variable with api.ReadBaoVariable and skip the test with the message "only running docker test when $BAO_BINARY present" when it is empty, so the Docker test never runs without an explicit binary."

### third-party-openbao-internal-vault-external-tests-namespaces

- intent: "" -> "This context exists to specify the black-box behavior the external namespace tests assert about OpenBao: how namespace deletion must survive an interrupted (cancelled) deletion and leave a tainted namespace that a second delete can finish, and how per-namespace seal/unseal state must propagate across all cores of a cluster, including after seal, step-down, restart and resync. It documents the acceptance rules these integration tests enforce so that changes to namespace deletion, tainting or namespace sealing can be checked against them."
- added `r.ci-skip-for-repeated-deletion` (MUST): "TestNamespaceRepeatedDeletion skips itself when the CI environment variable is non-empty, because creating 500 KV and userpass objects causes context cancellation timeouts, and otherwise runs in parallel."
- added `r.deletion-completes-and-clears-storage` (MUST): "Once the second delete is issued, sys/namespaces must become empty within the eventual timeout, and listing sys/raw/namespaces/<uuid> for the deleted namespace must return nil, showing namespace storage is gone."
- added `r.deletion-interrupted-leaves-tainted-namespace` (MUST): "After the namespace is deleted and the active core is stepped down, the namespace must still appear under sys/namespaces, a read of sys/namespaces/ns1 must report tainted true, and a second delete must be accepted."
- added `r.namespace-population-uses-v2-kv-and-userpass` (MUST): "Namespace population must enable KV-v2 mounts named kv-v2, kv-v1 and kv under the kv logical backend factory plus userpass credential backend, wait for the KV-v2 mount config to expose cas_required before writing entries, and write entries and users concurrently in the namespace of the admin policy."
- added `r.sealed-namespace-creation-returns-shares` (MUST): "Creating a namespace with a seal configuration must return a response carrying key_shares, and the Shamir configuration with shares 3 and threshold 2 must yield 3 share strings."
- added `r.sealed-state-on-every-node` (MUST): "A sealed namespace must reject mount listing with an error containing "is sealed" and a nil mount list on every core of the cluster, and an unsealed namespace must list non-empty mounts without error."
- added `r.three-core-cluster-with-eventual-checks` (MUST): "TestNamespaceClusterSealing runs a three-core test cluster in parallel and uses eventual assertions with 25 second timeouts and 100 millisecond polling for namespace creation, unsealing and resealing, because standby nodes can lag behind."
- added `r.unseal-and-seal-propagate-across-cluster` (MUST): "Unsealing a namespace from any core must unseal it immediately on the active core and eventually on all other nodes, and sealing a namespace must make it sealed again on all nodes."
- added `r.unsealed-state-resyncs-after-restart` (MUST): "After cores are sealed, stepped down and unsealed, namespaces that were unsealed must become reachable again on all nodes, showing unsealed namespace state is synchronized when nodes rejoin."

### third-party-openbao-internal-vault-external-tests-plugin

- intent: "" -> "The context exists to verify that OpenBao can build, register, mount, use, reload and recover external plugins across all supported plugin protocol versions and plugin types, and that plugin-related audit records carry the metadata needed to identify an externally mounted plugin. It is the integration-level safety net for the plugin catalog, plugin multiplexing, plugin lifecycle on seal/unseal and reload, and the audit enrichment of plugin mounts, so that changes to those subsystems fail loudly in CI instead of at an operator's deployment."
- added `r.audit-plugin-metadata` (MUST): "When a file audit backend is enabled, audit records for requests and responses on an external auth or secret plugin mount must contain mount_class equal to the plugin type string, mount_is_external_plugin as boolean true, and mount_running_sha256 as a string."
- added `r.auto-reload-on-rpc-error` (MUST): "A read of the mock plugin's errors/rpc path must return an error and must reset the backend's in-memory internal value, proving automatic reload after an RPC failure."
- added `r.continue-on-error` (MUST): "The external plugin continue-on-error test runs all four combinations of failure kind (sha256 mismatch via catalog update, missing binary via file removal) and plugin type (secret, auth), then seals and unseals, recompiles and re-registers the plugin, and requires that the previously failed unmount or auth disable now succeeds."
- added `r.database-plugin-postgres` (MUST): "The database plugin test mounts an external database secrets engine, prepares a PostgreSQL 13.4-buster test container with a vault user, writes a connection config bound to the plugin name, rotates the root credential, creates a role from the templated creation statements, generates credentials, and requires that a lease lookup succeeds before revocation and fails after it."
- added `r.database-reload-skipped` (SHOULD): "TestExternalPlugin_DatabaseReload skips with the message that reloading database plugins is not yet supported, so database reload remains explicitly unsupported until that skip is removed."
- added `r.missing-binary-and-catalog-removal` (MUST): "Removing the plugin binary from the cluster temp directory and unsealing must make a later read of sys/mounts/mock-0/tune fail, and deleting the plugin from the catalog, sealing and unsealing must leave the cluster active; when the test re-adds the plugin and mounts it on the still-existing path, that mount must fail."
- added `r.mock-plugin-entrypoints` (MUST): "The mock plugin entrypoints serve only when the SDK's plugin version environment variable is set, require the CA cert variable to be non-empty, parse the ca-cert flag, and dispatch to lplugin.Serve or lplugin.ServeMultiplex with a mock factory for the logical or credential backend type; the V4 variants additionally return early when AutoMTLS is enabled and install a TLSProviderFunc."
- added `r.multiplexed-shared-process` (MUST): "The auth-method and secrets-engine tests mount five instances of the same plugin in parallel subtests and complete a full lifecycle on each (configuration, credential or secret-id generation, login or read, renew and revoke or deregister), which requires the mounts to share a single multiplexed plugin process."
- added `r.package-is-external-test-package` (MUST): "Both files declare package plugin_test so the tests exercise the internal vault, http and builtin plugin packages only through their exported API."
- added `r.plugin-env-delivery` (MUST): "The env test mounts a plugin registered with FOO=BAR in its environment and the mock plugin entrypoint fails unless os.Getenv("FOO") equals BAR, confirming the plugin process receives the configured environment alongside the CA certificate variable."
- added `r.plugin-version-matrix` (MUST): "Plugin behaviour is asserted for each protocol generation by the logicalVersionMap and credentialVersionMap tables, whose keys v4, v5 and v5_multiplexed select the mock plugin entrypoint (V4, plain Serve, or ServeMultiplex) that the test registers for that generation."
- added `r.register-and-enable-both-plugin-types` (MUST): "The shared helpers register a compiled plugin in the catalog with its name, type, command, sha256 and version, then enable it either as a secrets mount (Sys().Mount) for consts.PluginTypeSecrets or as an auth method (Sys().EnableAuthWithOptions) for consts.PluginTypeCredential, and fail the test on any error."
- added `r.reload-keeps-plugin-usable` (MUST): "After a credential or secret plugin is registered, configured and used, calling ReloadPlugin on it must succeed and the same auth method or secret read must still work, after which the plugin is deregistered."
- added `r.reload-resets-plugin-state` (MUST): "Reload is asserted both on the per-plugin endpoint and on the sys/plugins/reload/backend endpoint: after writing an internal value of baz and issuing the reload (by plugin name or by mounts list), a subsequent read must return a value other than baz and the backend endpoint response must carry a non-nil reload_id."
- added `r.survive-seal-unseal` (MUST): "Tests for secret and auth plugins lazily load the mount, seal every core, unseal with all barrier keys, assert the core is not sealed, and wait for active so post-unseal plugin restoration is proven to complete."

### third-party-openbao-internal-vault-external-tests-policy

- intent: "" -> "The context exists so the templated-policy and policy-pagination behaviour of the Vault core can be described and verified end to end from outside the vault package. The tests encode the observable contract of the HTTP policy surface: what a login or renewal response must report for token, identity, and combined policy sets; how pagination_limit and required_parameters on an ACL path constrain list and scan operations; when identity template values resolve versus deny; and how policy data propagates to a standby core when the cache is disabled. The LDAP-auth block stays commented out because it needs an LDAP plugin and container, so the remaining tests use userpass and the built-in KV backend only."
- added `r.bad-group-template-isolated` (MUST): "A policy that references a non-existent group through a name template MUST NOT prevent the other paths in the token's policy set from working. Installing badPolicy1, which templates identity.groups.names.foobar.name, MUST leave every other templated path behaving exactly as it did before, so only the unresolvable-template path is affected."
- added `r.disabled-cache-policy-invalidation` (MUST): "TestPolicyStore_DisabledCacheInvalidation MUST start a two-core cluster with DisableCache true, create a namespace, and write a read-only policy through the active core. It MUST then retry for up to 10 seconds against the standby core's GetPolicy until the returned policy text is byte-identical to the text that was written, so that policy writes invalidate on a standby when no cache is present."
- added `r.group-membership-flips-template` (MUST): "Adding the entity to the previously empty foobar group MUST make the path templated on that group name resolve: a write to secret/foobar/foo that was denied before the membership change MUST succeed afterwards."
- added `r.identity-template-resolution` (MUST): "TestPolicyTemplating MUST accept identity-templated paths over entity name, entity metadata keys, group names, group ids, and alias names. Given an entity named entity_name with metadata key=metadata, a group named group_name containing that entity, a group named foobar, and a userpass alias named testuser, writes to secret/entity_name/foo, secret/group_name/foo, secret/<groupID>/foo, secret/testuser/foo and secret/metadata/test/foo MUST succeed, while a write to secret/entityname/foo MUST be denied."
- added `r.invalid-metadata-rejected` (MUST): "Entity metadata whose value contains template-breaking characters, a wildcard, MUST make every templated path in the policy fail. Rewriting the same policy with allow_wildcards_in_identity_templates and allow_slashes_in_identity_templates both true MUST restore access without changing the metadata."
- added `r.ldap-backed-tests-disabled` (SHOULD): "The LDAP-backed no-default-policy and no-configured-policy tests SHOULD remain commented out with their rationale recorded, so the package compiles and runs without an LDAP plugin or container while the intended coverage stays visible."
- added `r.pagination-assertion-helper` (MUST): "The testPagination helper MUST assert, for a given metadata sub-path, that a raw list returns 100 keys when the path is unpaginated or at most 10 when paginated and errors when the path is not raw-listable, that a list page of 75 errors when the path is paginated and otherwise returns exactly 75 keys, and that a list page of 10 always succeeds with at most 10 keys. The limited and raw arguments decide which of these assertions apply."
- added `r.policy-pagination-limits` (MUST): "TestPolicy_PaginationLimit MUST mount a versioned KV backend and write 100 keys under each of the a, b, c and d prefixes, then write a policy where kv/metadata/a allows list with no pagination limit, kv/metadata/b allows list with pagination_limit 10, kv/metadata/c allows list with required_parameters ["limit"] but no pagination limit, kv/metadata/d allows list with both pagination_limit 10 and required_parameters ["limit"], and kv/metadata/ allows scan and list with both settings. A raw list MUST return all 100 keys on a, c and the no-suffix path, and at most 10 keys on b; raw list on d MUST fail. A list with limit=max or limit=0 MUST return 10 keys where a pagination limit applies and 100 keys where none applies, and limit=-1 MUST fail with "permission denied". Scan without limits MUST error, scan with a page size of 10 MUST succeed and return 400 keys because KV metadata scanning does not paginate."
- added `r.token-policy-renewal-composition` (MUST): "TestPolicy_TokenRenewal MUST run four table cases (no policies, token policies only, identity policies only, both) by enabling the userpass auth backend, optionally setting token_policies on the user, optionally creating an identity entity with policies plus an entity-alias bound through the userpass mount accessor, and logging in. The login response MUST report Auth.TokenPolicies equal to the token policies with "default" prepended, Auth.IdentityPolicies equal to the configured identity policies, and Auth.Policies equal to the concatenation of both. After a renew through auth/token/renew the same three sets MUST be reported unchanged."

### third-party-openbao-internal-vault-external-tests-postgresql-binary

- intent: "" -> "The context exists to exercise the PostgreSQL storage backend of OpenBao against real containerised server binaries instead of in-memory storage, so that lock fencing, concurrent initialization, initialization failure, rolling upgrades and primary/replica failover are all covered end to end. It is an external, opt-in test suite: it needs Docker plus a compiled binary supplied through BAO_BINARY, and it skips otherwise so the ordinary unit test run stays fast and dependency-free."
- added `r.fatal-init` (MUST): "TestPostgreSQL_FatalInit must build the cluster directly through docker.NewDockerCluster with a single core, SkipInit true, an explicit cluster name derived from the test name and SkipStorageCleanup true, supply the failing self-init-failure.hcl fixture alongside the good ones, and require an error from the call; it must then swap the fixture set back to the working self-init.hcl and static-seal.hcl and require that startup is still refused with an error."
- added `r.fenced-writes` (MUST): "TestPostgreSQL_FencedWrites must start a PostgreSQL-backed Docker cluster from the supplied binary, spam ten goroutines that each write sys/policies/acl/custom up to five hundred times with a 5ms pause, then delete every row from the openbao_ha_locks table through the storage client and require that at least one goroutine observed an error containing physical.ErrFencedWriteFailed; after a six second pause it must require testcluster.WaitForActiveNode to find a new active node and require that a repeat write on that node succeeds with a nil response."
- added `r.package-and-binary-gate` (MUST): "The file must declare package raft_binary, and every test must read the BAO_BINARY environment variable via api.ReadBaoVariable and call t.Skip when the value is empty, so no test reaches Docker unless a server binary path is supplied."
- added `r.parallel-init` (MUST): "TestPostgreSQL_ParallelInit must copy the self-init.hcl and static-seal.hcl fixtures into the cluster config path, start with SkipInit set, require that the first node reports Initialized true and Sealed false, log in as admin through auth/userpass to adopt the returned auth token as the cluster root token, and then require that every node answers ListPoliciesWithContext within ten seconds so the count of active nodes equals the node count."
- added `r.rolling-upgrade` (MUST): "TestPostgreSQL_Upgrade must first start a three node cluster on the published latest image with no binary override, mount a version 2 kv secrets engine, write the value known-value at a/key and wait for the write to succeed, then set VaultBinary on the options and call node.Upgrade on every node under a sixty second timeout; afterwards it must wait for an active node and require that reading a/key returns known-value again."
- added `r.scalability-failover` (MUST): "TestPostgreSQL_Scalability must build a PostgreSQL cluster storage with a node mapper that places the first two nodes on the primary, adds a replica for the third index and points later indices at the first replica, then start a three core OpenBao cluster with audit logging to stdout and trace level; it must verify a kv version 2 value is read identically from every node with client redirects disabled, and then in order require that sealing the primary lets a secondary accept writes, that the value propagates to the third node, that sealing the secondary makes the read-only third node fail with 'local node not active but active cluster node not found', that UnsealAllNodes restores identical reads everywhere, that removing the PostgreSQL primary makes writes and reads on the first node fail within thirty seconds, that the third node eventually reads the last written value, and that PromoteNode on the replica lets the remaining nodes write and read post-failover-known-value."

### third-party-openbao-internal-vault-external-tests-pprof

- intent: "" -> "This context exists to specify the external pprof verification surface of the vendored OpenBao tree, so the pprof endpoints of a running Vault-compatible cluster stay covered by tests that live outside the core packages. It pins down what the two exported entrypoints must do to a live cluster: which pprof paths get exercised, how the requests are configured, which responses count as failures, and that the standby node is probed directly alongside the active node. It is written for readers who need to know the contract of these exported test helpers without reading the vendored source."
- added `r.http-client-tls-http2` (MUST): "The requests must go through an HTTP client built on cleanhttp's default pooled transport carrying the first node's TLS config, configured for HTTP/2, and any transport configuration error must fail the test."
- added `r.pprof-response-validation` (MUST): "Each pprof response body must be read in full; an unmarshal error is ignored because some endpoints return binary blobs, but a response whose decoded JSON contains an errors key must fail the test with that error value, and an empty body must fail the test."
- added `r.profile-trace-seconds-param` (MUST): "The profile and trace cases must send a seconds parameter of 1, and cases whose seconds value is empty must send no seconds parameter at all."
- added `r.standby-both-nodes-cmdline` (MUST): "SysPprof_Standby_Test must read sys/pprof/cmdline as a raw logical response from node 0 and then node 1 of the cluster, requiring no error and a non-empty command line from each and logging both values."
- added `r.sys-pprof-endpoint-sweep` (MUST): "SysPprof_Test must exercise the sys/pprof endpoints index, cmdline, goroutine, heap, profile, symbol and trace, issuing one GET request per case against the first node of the cluster and running each as its own subtest named after the case."
- added `r.test-wiring` (SHOULD): "The Go tests in pprof_test.go should call the exported helpers with a freshly created test cluster, so TestSysPprof drives SysPprof_Test and TestSysPprof_Standby drives SysPprof_Standby_Test."

### third-party-openbao-internal-vault-external-tests-pprof-pprof-binary

- intent: "" -> "This context exists to verify that the sys/pprof endpoints behave the same way on a real OpenBao server process as they do on the fake test cluster used by the sibling pprof package. The two tests are deliberately thin: they only build the exec dev cluster, wire the binary path and listen address, and hand the cluster to the shared pprof test bodies, because the mechanism under test is the exec-based cluster, not the pprof assertions themselves. The BAO_BINARY gate keeps the suite from failing on machines without a built server binary."
- added `r.assertions-delegated` (SHOULD): "The package holds no pprof assertions of its own; the pprof response checks stay in the imported pprof package and are reached only through pprof.SysPprof_Test and pprof.SysPprof_Standby_Test, so the exec wrapper stays a thin transport-swap layer over the in-process tests."
- added `r.binary-env-gate` (MUST): "Both tests read BAO_BINARY through api.ReadBaoVariable and call t.Skip with "only running exec test when $BAO_BINARY present" when the value is empty, so no cluster is started and no pprof assertion runs without a server binary; there are no command-line flags in this package."
- added `r.cluster-cleanup-deferred` (MUST): "Each test defers cluster.Cleanup() immediately after the cluster is created, so the spawned server process tree is torn down on pass, fail, or skip of the delegated pprof test."
- added `r.exec-dev-cluster-for-pprof` (MUST): "TestSysPprof_Exec runs in parallel and, when the BAO_BINARY variable is non-empty, builds a dev cluster through testcluster.NewTestExecDevCluster with ClusterOptions.NumCores set to 1, BinaryPath taken from BAO_BINARY, and BaseListenAddress 127.0.0.1:8208, then calls pprof.SysPprof_Test with that cluster."
- added `r.standby-exec-dev-cluster` (MUST): "TestSysPprof_Standby_Exec runs in parallel and, when BAO_BINARY is non-empty, builds an exec dev cluster with VaultNodeConfig.DisablePerformanceStandby set to true, BinaryPath from BAO_BINARY, and BaseListenAddress 127.0.0.1:8210, then calls pprof.SysPprof_Standby_Test with that cluster."

### third-party-openbao-internal-vault-external-tests-quotas

- intent: "" -> "The context exists to pin down the externally observable contract of the OpenBao rate-limit quota subsystem as demanded by its external_tests/quotas package: how quota rules are named and deduplicated, how they bind to paths, mounts and namespaces, how child namespaces inherit them when the inheritable flag is set, how configured and default exempt paths bypass them, how enforcement tracks the token-bucket refill rate, how violations are written to the audit log, and how a mount-scoped rule takes precedence over a root-scoped one. Because the package is test-only and exports nothing but test entrypoints, the specification is expressed as invariants the tests require of the vault core and quota engine rather than as callable production API."
- added `r.audit-logging` (MUST): "With enable_rate_limit_audit_logging true in sys/quotas/config and the file audit backend enabled, a first request must pass and a second request under a 1 RPS quota must fail with an error containing 429, and the audit log must contain exactly one request-type record whose error field ends with quotas.ErrRateLimitQuotaExceeded."
- added `r.cluster-fixture` (MUST): "Each test must build its own in-memory Vault cluster from teststorage.ClusterSetup with coreConfig, start it, wait for active with vault.TestWaitActive, and defer cluster.Cleanup; coreConfig must register the pki logical backend, the userpass credential backend and the file audit backend."
- added `r.default-exempt-health` (MUST): "With a rate-limit quota of 1 RPS in force, two consecutive reads of sys/health must both succeed and return non-nil responses with non-nil data, because sys/health belongs to the default exempt paths."
- added `r.duplicate-name` (MUST): "Writing a rate-limit quota at sys/quotas/rate-limit/secret-rlq twice under the same name with different paths must succeed and leave exactly one entry returned by listing sys/quotas/rate-limit."
- added `r.duplicate-path` (MUST): "Creating a second rate-limit quota whose path collides with an existing quota's path (for example a global quota with empty path, then another empty-path quota) must be rejected with an error, and reading a quota by name must return non-empty data."
- added `r.exempt-paths` (MUST): "Default configuration read from sys/quotas/config must report a non-empty rate_limit_exempt_paths list; with a 7.7 RPS quota some requests must fail and successes must not exceed ceil(8 + 7.7*elapsedSeconds) + 1; after writing rate_limit_exempt_paths containing sys/quotas/rate-limit and allowing one second for refill, every request must succeed and none must fail."
- added `r.global-quota` (MUST): "A global rate-limit quota of 7.7 RPS must cause some requests to fail with successes bounded by ceil(8 + 7.7*elapsedSeconds) + 1; after one second of refill and an update to 10000 RPS, no further request may fail."
- added `r.inheritable-toggle` (MUST): "A quota on path ns1 with inheritable true at 7.7 RPS must apply to the child namespace ns1/ns1.1 so some requests there fail; after the same quota is rewritten with inheritable false, requests inside ns1/ns1.1 must all succeed while requests in ns1 must again fail under the same success bound."
- added `r.mount-fixture` (MUST): "setupMounts must enable a userpass auth mount with user foo password bar, mount pki, generate an internal root certificate with common_name testvault.com, ttl 200h and ip_sans 127.0.0.1, and create role test with require_cn false, allowed_domains testvault.com, allow_subdomains true, max_ttl 2h and generate_lease true; teardownMounts must unmount pki and disable the userpass and approle auth mounts, failing the test on any error."
- added `r.mount-precedence` (MUST): "When a root rate-limit quota of 14.7 RPS and a pki/-scoped quota of 7.7 RPS both exist, the pki/-scoped quota must take precedence: some pki requests must fail and successes must stay at or below the bound computed from 7.7 RPS, not from 14.7."
- added `r.mount-quota` (MUST): "A rate-limit quota with path pki/ at 7.7 RPS must reject some requests while keeping successes at or below ceil(8 + 7.7*elapsedSeconds) + 1; after updating the same quota to 10000 RPS no request may fail; teardownMounts must then remove the mounts."
- added `r.namespace-quota` (MUST): "A global inheritable quota of 7.7 RPS must bound requests issued from the root and from namespace ns1, while a quota declared at path ns1/ns1.1 with 9.9 RPS must allow more requests, bounded by ceil(10 + 9.9*elapsedSeconds) + 1, when listing sys/namespaces inside ns1/ns1.1."
- added `r.response-schema-validation` (SHOULD): "Tests that opt in by setting RequestResponseCallback to schema.ResponseValidatingCallback must have every API response validated against the registered response schema; tests that disable default quotas set NoDefaultQuotas to keep the fixture free of built-in quota rules."
- added `r.rps-harness` (MUST): "testRPS and testRPSWithNS must call the supplied request function in a tight loop until the given duration elapses, counting successes and failures in atomic counters, optionally setting and clearing a namespace per call, and must return the success count, the failure count and the elapsed wall-clock duration."

### third-party-openbao-internal-vault-external-tests-raft

- intent: "" -> "This context exists so that the raft external tests have a reusable, cluster-agnostic assertion for Raft configuration state instead of each test spelling out the sys/storage/raft/configuration parse and leader checks itself. The helper parameterizes the cluster as a testcluster.VaultCluster, so any cluster implementation the test suite builds can be handed to it, and it derives the expected membership from cluster.Nodes() rather than from a literal list, which keeps the expectation correct as the node count changes. The two test files exist to invoke that helper (TestRaft_Configuration) and to exercise autopilot behavior against the same cluster shape; the context is defined by the shared assertion, not by the individual test names."
- added `r.helper-reused-by-suite` (SHOULD): "The assertion lives in raft.go and is driven from the package's test files: raft_test.go calls Raft_Configuration_Test from TestRaft_Configuration, so the helper stays free of test-registration side effects and remains callable by other tests in third_party/openbao/internal/vault/external_tests/raft/raft_autopilot_test.go and raft_test.go."
- added `r.leader-is-core-0` (MUST): "For every server entry in secret.Data["config"]["servers"], the helper reads node_id and leader; the entry whose node_id is core-0 must have leader true, and every other entry must have leader false. A violation fails the test with t.Fatalf carrying the offending server value."
- added `r.membership-matches-node-count` (MUST): "The helper builds the set of observed node_id values and an expected set of names core-0 through core-(N-1), where N is len(cluster.Nodes()), and fails the test when deep.Equal between the two sets returns a non-empty diff, reporting the diff with t.Fatalf."
- added `r.reads-raft-configuration` (MUST): "Raft_Configuration_Test takes a *testing.T and a testcluster.VaultCluster, takes the API client of the cluster's first node via cluster.Nodes()[0].APIClient(), and reads the path sys/storage/raft/configuration with Logical().Read; a read error is reported with t.Fatal and stops the test."

### third-party-openbao-internal-vault-external-tests-raft-raft-binary

- intent: "" -> "This context exists so the raft configuration behaviour exercised by the shared external raft test suite is also covered against real docker-hosted vault nodes driven by a locally built binary, rather than only in-process nodes. It guards the join and reconfiguration path: the cluster must behave correctly both before and after a node is added, and the test only runs where a binary path is supplied, so developers without docker or a built binary get a skip instead of a failure."
- added `r.config-test-before-and-after-add-node` (MUST): "rafttest.Raft_Configuration_Test runs against the cluster once before cluster.AddNode, and again after AddNode succeeds; AddNode is called with the context from t.Context() and the same options value, and a non-nil error return fails the test with t.Fatal and prevents the second run."
- added `r.docker-cluster-options` (MUST): "The cluster is built from a docker.DockerClusterOptions value with ImageRepo "quay.io/openbao/openbao", ImageTag "latest", VaultBinary set to the BAO_BINARY value, and ClusterOptions.VaultNodeConfig.LogLevel "TRACE", then that options value is passed to docker.NewTestDockerCluster along with the testing.T."
- added `r.parallel-and-cleanup` (MUST): "The test calls t.Parallel() before any other setup, and defers cluster.Cleanup() immediately after docker.NewTestDockerCluster returns, so docker clusters do not leak when the test fails or is skipped over later."
- added `r.skip-without-binary` (MUST): "TestRaft_Configuration_Docker reads api.ReadBaoVariable("BAO_BINARY") into a binary variable and calls t.Skip with the message "only running docker test when $BAO_BINARY present" when that variable is empty, so the docker test runs only where a binary path is provided."

### third-party-openbao-internal-vault-external-tests-raftha

- intent: "" -> "This context exists to pin down the raft HA external tests of the vendored OpenBao tree: they exercise cluster formation over two physical backends and two TLS client-certificate modes, and they exercise growing an existing non-raft cluster into a raft-HA cluster while preserving barrier keys and the root token. It records what the tests set up and assert so that the join, peer-verification and peer-removal behaviour they depend on stays specified."
- added `r.bootstrap-and-join-upgraded-cluster` (MUST): "In the upgraded cluster the leader client must set the saved root token, seal the leader to install the address provider and unseal it again, write sys/storage/raft/bootstrap to make the leader active, install the address provider on the other two cores' raft backends, join cores 1 and 2 with the cluster CA certificate, and verify all three cores are peers."
- added `r.cluster-setup-three-cores` (MUST): "testRaftHANewCluster must configure a vault.CoreConfig and vault.TestClusterOptions through teststorage.RaftHASetup with vaulthttp.Handler, start a three-core vault test cluster, and clean it up on exit."
- added `r.existing-cluster-upgrade` (MUST): "TestRaft_HA_ExistingCluster must create a cluster with raft absent as HA backend (physBundle.HABackend set to nil) over reusable in-memory storage, capture the cluster barrier keys and root token, then build a second cluster over reusable raft HA storage with SkipInit true and restore those captured barrier keys and root token onto it."
- added `r.join-cores` (MUST): "Cores 1 and 2 must join through api.RaftJoinRequest carrying the cluster CA certificate as LeaderCACert, and when addClientCerts is true also carrying LeaderClientCert and LeaderClientKey from the cluster CA material; a join error or a response with Joined false must fail the test."
- added `r.leader-address-provider` (MUST): "The leader core must be sealed before a testhelpers.TestRaftServerAddressProvider is installed on its raft.RaftBackend, then unsealed, and the test must wait for the core to become active; this ordering exists because the address provider can only be swapped while the core is sealed."
- added `r.new-cluster-matrix` (MUST): "TestRaft_HA_NewCluster must run four parallel subtests: the file backend and the in-memory backend, each with and without client certificates, and each must delegate to testRaftHANewCluster with the matching teststorage bundler and addClientCerts flag."
- added `r.remove-peer` (MUST): "Writing sys/storage/raft/remove-peer with server_id core-1 and then core-2 against the leader client must succeed, and a following testhelpers.VerifyRaftPeers must confirm core-0 is the only remaining peer."
- added `r.test-cluster-options-existing` (SHOULD): "The existing-cluster test should run with performance standby disabled, standbys kept sealed, and standby reads disabled, and should name its logger after the test for readable output."
- added `r.verify-peers-added` (MUST): "After joining, testhelpers.VerifyRaftPeers on the leader client must confirm core-0, core-1 and core-2 are all present as peers."

### third-party-openbao-internal-vault-external-tests-response

- intent: "" -> "This context exists to pin down the observable contract of the response-header allow-list in the vendored third_party/openbao vault HTTP handler, independent of this repository's own code: a plugin mount must not be able to leak arbitrary HTTP response headers to clients, and an operator must be able to opt a specific header back in per mount through the allowed_response_headers tuning, including when the configured casing differs from the emitted casing. Because the file is an external black-box test that speaks only over the HTTP API (client.Logical().ReadRaw, client.Sys().TuneMount) and not over internal Go packages, it documents the behaviour the vendored handler is expected to preserve across upstream updates rather than behaviour authored in this repo."
- added `r.allowed-response-headers-tuning` (MUST): "After client.Sys().TuneMount("auth/headtest", api.MountConfigInput{AllowedResponseHeaders: []string{"WwW-AuthenTicate"}}), the www-authenticate header value Negotiate must appear on both the 200 response from auth/headtest/loginnoerror and the 401 response from auth/headtest/login, so the allowed-list comparison must ignore letter case."
- added `r.credential-mount-header-emission` (MUST): "The test registers a credential backend named headtest whose login and loginnoerror read callbacks each return a logical.Response carrying Headers map[string][]string with key www-authenticate and value Negotiate; login additionally returns logical.CodedError(401, "authentication required") and loginnoerror returns an empty logical.Auth with a nil error. The backend is mounted through the API as auth type headtest on a test cluster built from vault.CoreConfig with that factory."
- added `r.headers-stripped-when-not-allowed` (MUST): "When the mount has not been tuned, reading auth/headtest/loginnoerror must return HTTP status 200 with an empty www-authenticate header, and reading auth/headtest/login must return an error with HTTP status 401 and an empty www-authenticate header; the test fails if any of these headers is present."
- added `r.raw-response-inspection` (SHOULD): "Header assertions must inspect the raw HTTP response through client.Logical().ReadRaw, which returns the status code and the header collection directly rather than the decoded logical response."
- added `r.test-cluster-lifecycle` (MUST): "The test must run against a vault.NewTestCluster configured with HandlerFunc vaulthttp.Handler and DisableStandbyReads true, start it with cluster.Start(), wait for the active core with vault.TestWaitActive, and defer cluster.Cleanup() so the cluster is always torn down."

### third-party-openbao-internal-vault-external-tests-router

- intent: "" -> "The context exists to pin down router behavior that only shows up end to end: how mounts at nested subpaths resolve regardless of the order they are created, how they survive a seal/unseal cycle, and that a mount whose rollback function returns an error can still be reloaded and remounted. It is an external test package, so it is written against the api/v2 client and the HTTP handler, which keeps it decoupled from internal router types and guards the wiring between HTTP routing, core mount bookkeeping, and backend lifecycle."
- added `r.mount-subpath-order-independence` (MUST): "Mounting an auth backend and a secrets backend at nested subpath mount points must succeed whether the longer mounted path is created before or after the shorter one; the test runs the pair {"a/abcd/123", "abcd/123"} in both orders against a fresh cluster."
- added `r.mount-subpath-seal-unseal` (MUST): "After the auth and secrets backends are mounted at their subpaths, all cores in the cluster must seal and then unseal successfully, with a failure reported through the test rather than ignored."
- added `r.noop-backend-factory-source` (MUST): "The failing-rollback test must mount the noop backend built from backend.NoopBackendRollbackErrFactory so the periodic rollback error is produced by the mounted backend itself."
- added `r.reload-backend-with-failing-rollback` (MUST): "Reloading a mounted backend whose periodic rollback function returns an error must succeed: a write to sys/plugins/reload/backend for that mount must not return an error."
- added `r.remount-backend-with-failing-rollback` (MUST): "Remounting a backend whose periodic rollback function returns an error must succeed: a write to sys/remount moving that mount to a new path must not return an error, and the cores must then seal and unseal."
- added `r.router-tests-use-http-handler-and-real-cluster` (MUST): "Both tests must build the cluster with vault.NewTestCluster using vaulthttp.Handler as the handler func, wait for the first core to become active, drive it through cluster.Cores[0].Client, and clean the cluster up on exit."

### third-party-openbao-internal-vault-external-tests-sealmigration

- intent: "" -> "The package exists so OpenBao's seal-migration behavior can be exercised end to end against real test clusters. Each ParamTest* function is a scenario that a caller's test file invokes, parameterized by logger, reusable storage and a base port, so the same migration logic runs over different storage backends. The pre-1.4 and post-1.4 variants exist because the migration protocol changed at that version, and the transit-to-transit variant covers moving between two transit seals."
- added `r.initialize-transit` (MUST): "InitializeTransit must build a test cluster whose seal is a transit seal backed by the given TransitSealServer and seal key name, and must return both the started cluster and the TestClusterOptions used to create it so callers can reach the seal and unwrap seal functions."
- added `r.parameterized-scenarios` (MUST): "Every ParamTest* scenario must accept the same parameter set — *testing.T, hclog.Logger, teststorage.ReusableStorage and an int base port — so a caller can run each scenario against any reusable storage backend with its own logger and port."
- added `r.shamir-to-transit-post14` (MUST): "ParamTestSealMigrationShamirToTransit_Post14 must initialize a shamir cluster, start a transit server with key transit-seal-key-1, replace opts.SealFunc with one that builds a seal from that transit server, run the post-1.4 migration with the barrier keys as recovery keys, validate that the seal configuration is transit, then run the cluster in autoseal mode."
- added `r.shamir-to-transit-pre14` (MUST): "ParamTestSealMigrationShamirToTransit_Pre14 must initialize a cluster with shamir, capture root token and barrier keys, start a transit seal server holding key transit-seal-key-1, run the pre-1.4 shamir-to-transit migration where the barrier keys become recovery keys, then run the cluster in autoseal mode with the returned seal function."
- added `r.test-files-invoke-shared-scenarios` (SHOULD): "The package's test files should invoke the shared parameterized scenarios rather than reimplementing migration steps, with seal_migration_pre14_test.go covering the pre-1.4 path and seal_migration_test.go covering the post-1.4 and transit-to-transit paths."
- added `r.transit-to-shamir-post14` (MUST): "ParamTestSealMigrationTransitToShamir_Post14 must initialize a transit-sealed cluster, move the existing SealFunc into UnwrapSealFunc and set SealFunc to return nil, run the post-1.4 migration with the recovery keys, validate that the resulting seal configuration is shamir, then stop the transit server and run the cluster with shamir."
- added `r.transit-to-shamir-pre14` (MUST): "ParamTestSealMigrationTransitToShamir_Pre14 must start a transit seal server, create the key named transit-seal-key, initialize a cluster sealed with transit, ensure its cores are sealed, run the pre-1.4 transit-to-shamir migration, then stop the transit server and run the cluster with shamir using the former recovery keys as barrier keys."
- added `r.transit-to-transit` (MUST): "ParamTestSealMigration_TransitToTransit must exercise a seal migration from one transit seal to another, taking the logger, reusable storage and base port a caller supplies."

### third-party-openbao-internal-vault-external-tests-sealmigrationext

- intent: "" -> "This context exists so the seal-migration scenarios that the shared internal/vault/external_tests/sealmigration package implements can be driven from a thin external test surface without duplicating the scenario bodies. The file supplies the concrete test entrypoints for Shamir-to-Transit, Transit-to-Shamir and Transit-to-Transit migration, split across the pre-1.4 and post-1.4 variants, and it fixes the per-test in-memory storage construction and the base-port offset that keeps the parallel tests from colliding on listening ports."
- added `r.base-port-offset` (MUST): "Every test must pass a port derived from a sealmigration base-port constant plus 300: BasePort_ShamirToTransit_Pre14 for the pre-1.4 Shamir-to-Transit test, BasePort_TransitToShamir_Pre14 for the pre-1.4 Transit-to-Shamir test, BasePort_TransitToShamir_Post14 for the post-1.4 Transit-to-Shamir test and BasePort_TransitToTransit for the Transit-to-Transit test, so parallel runs on shared storage do not collide on listening ports."
- added `r.debug-named-logger` (MUST): "Each test must build its logger with logging.NewVaultLogger at hclog.Debug level and rename it with t.Name(), so log records carry the test name."
- added `r.delegate-to-sealmigration` (MUST): "Each test must delegate the scenario body to the matching parameterized helper in the sealmigration package, passing the logger, the storage handle and a base port, rather than implementing migration steps itself."
- added `r.distinct-scenarios` (MUST): "The package must expose exactly five top-level tests, one for each seal-migration scenario: Shamir-to-Transit before 1.4, Transit-to-Shamir before 1.4, Shamir-to-Transit after 1.4, Transit-to-Shamir after 1.4 and Transit-to-Transit after 1.4."
- added `r.inmem-reusable-storage` (MUST): "Each test must obtain storage by calling teststorage.MakeReusableStorage with a backend produced by teststorage.MakeInmemBackend, and must defer the cleanup function that MakeReusableStorage returns so the storage is torn down when the test ends."
- added `r.parallel` (MUST): "Every test in the package must call t.Parallel() before doing any other work, so the scenarios run concurrently."
- added `r.post14-transit-to-shamir` (MUST): "TestSealMigration_TransitToShamir_Post14 must call sealmigration.ParamTestSealMigrationTransitToShamir_Post14 with BasePort_TransitToShamir_Post14 plus 300, mirroring the pre-1.4 Transit-to-Shamir test at a different port base."
- added `r.pre14-shamir-to-transit-wiring` (MUST): "TestSealMigration_ShamirToTransit_Pre14 must call sealmigration.ParamTestSealMigrationShamirToTransit_Pre14, while TestSealMigration_ShamirToTransit_Post14 must call sealmigration.ParamTestSealMigrationTransitToShamir_Post14, which is the helper the file actually wires to that test name."
- added `r.transit-to-transit` (SHOULD): "The Transit-to-Transit scenario must run only in its post-1.4 form, through sealmigration.ParamTestSealMigration_TransitToTransit, with no pre-1.4 counterpart in this package."

### third-party-openbao-internal-vault-external-tests-standby

- intent: "" -> "This context exists to pin down, as executable tests, the contract that a standby node in an OpenBao/Vault-style cluster remains readable: it serves read requests for data written on the primary, it must not accept a token that the primary has revoked, and write or wrapping operations it cannot serve locally must be refused with a forwarding error rather than handled. It lives under third_party/openbao as upstream external tests, so it exercises the public-ish surface (vault.NewTestCluster, Core.Standby, Core.HAState, Core.HandleRequest, logical.ShouldForward, teststorage.RaftBackendSetup, testhelpers.WaitForActiveNodeAndStandbys) rather than internals, and is kept so the deno-kcp repository inherits upstream regression coverage for standby semantics."
- added `r.active-core-serves-wrapping-standby-forwards` (MUST): "For a ReadOperation carrying logical.RequestWrapInfo with a 15 second TTL, a core whose HAState() is consts.Active must return no error and a non-nil response whose WrapInfo.TTL equals 15 seconds, while every other core must return an error for which logical.ShouldForward(err) is true."
- added `r.revoked-token-denied-on-standby` (MUST): "After the primary revokes the token tree, the standby client must eventually fail its KVv2 read with an error containing "permission denied", showing that secondary nodes honor revocation performed on the primary."
- added `r.standby-cluster-reaches-active-plus-standby` (MUST): "The test cluster must reach a state with an active node and standbys before assertions run: after cluster.Start() and testhelpers.WaitForActiveNodeAndStandbys, cluster.Cores[0].Standby() must be false, and cleanup must be registered via t.Cleanup(cluster.Cleanup)."
- added `r.standby-uses-forwarding-not-local-handling` (SHOULD): "Standby nodes should handle requests that they cannot serve themselves by returning a forwardable error rather than executing the request locally, so callers can detect the condition with logical.ShouldForward."
- added `r.writes-from-any-core-visible-on-primary-and-standby` (MUST): "A value written through any core's KVv2 client into the kv mount must become readable through both the primary client and the standby client, polled with require.EventuallyWithT at a 10 second timeout and 100 millisecond tick, with the exact per-core expected value compared against data.Data["bar"]."

### third-party-openbao-internal-vault-external-tests-storage-crosstest

- intent: "" -> "This context pins down the behavioural contract that OpenBao's logical.Storage implementations must satisfy collectively. The file is a conformance harness: any backend registered in allLogical or allTransactionalLogical must be indistinguishable from its peers under the same operation stream, so adding a storage backend means adding it to those maps and letting the shared assertions prove parity. It encodes the edge cases the project cares about — storage-root listing, prefix versus exact-key deletion, nil versus empty list results, write ordering, pagination with after and limit, and transactional conflict detection — as executable assertions rather than prose."
- added `r.backend-parity` (MUST): "Every backend in the map passed to exerciseBackends must return identical values for the same Get, Put, Delete, List and ListPage call, and deep.Equal differences must fail the test with a message naming the two backends and the differing items."
- added `r.backend-sets` (MUST): "allLogical must supply map entries named pure-raft, raft, raft-in-tx, file, inmem, inmem-via-wrapper, txinmem-via-wrapper and psql, each begun via logical.NewLogicalStorage over the corresponding physical backend, and allTransactionalLogical must supply raft, txinmem, inmem+sv, inmem+aes+sv, inmem+aes+bv, inmem+cache+encoding+aes+bv and raft+cache+encoding+aes+bv."
- added `r.error-parity` (MUST): "When shouldError is false each backend must return no error and when true each must return an error; the allDoSame* wrappers assert this per backend name before comparing results."
- added `r.listpage-semantics` (MUST): "ListPage must return at most limit entries sorted lexicographically past after, with limit of zero or a negative integer meaning unlimited; after need not exist; an after value beyond all keys returns nothing; and pagination must be tested exhaustively for ten sequentially created key-N entries."
- added `r.nil-empty-list-equal` (MUST): "A nil list result and an empty list result must be treated as equal; the list and list-page comparisons skip the deep.Equal check when both expected and actual have length zero, because the file backend returns an empty slice where other backends return nil."
- added `r.parallel-and-cleanup` (MUST): "Each top-level test must call t.Parallel, must defer the cleanup returned with the backend set, and must roll back every transaction-backed entry after exercising it so the shared raft and postgres resources are left usable."
- added `r.random-ops` (MUST): "getRandomOps must generate the configured operation counts (1000 for the non-transactional run, 1000 with a transaction limit of 10 for the transactional run) over the fixed file, folder, after and content operand sets, and the executors must serialize the ops to a JSON file under the system temporary directory, delete that file when the run finishes, and fail if any backend disagrees on error presence, list result or entry result."
- added `r.read-only-transaction` (MUST): "Put and Delete on a read-only transaction must fail while Commit of that same transaction must succeed, and listing the underlying storage afterwards must show no change."
- added `r.storage-semantics` (MUST): "The exercised storage contract must hold: the empty prefix is the root; Delete of a missing key succeeds; Get of a missing key returns a nil entry and no error; Put then Get returns the stored value; List of a key with children returns both the key and its trailing-slash subtree entry; Delete of a parent removes only the base entry and leaves children; repeated writes to one key return the last value even when shorter; and deleting all entries leaves no list artifacts."
- added `r.transaction-conflict` (MUST): "Two concurrent transactions that write the same key must conflict so the second terminal commit fails and the first committed value stands, including when both wrote byte-identical contents or one read then deleted the other's key; transactions writing disjoint keys must both commit and both values must be readable."
- added `r.transaction-lifecycle` (MUST): "A transaction begun by BeginTx or BeginReadOnlyTx that is committed or rolled back with no intervening operations must succeed once, and the same terminal operation repeated on the finished transaction must fail regardless of whether the second operation is Commit or Rollback or swaps between them."

### third-party-openbao-internal-vault-external-tests-tlslistener-binary

- intent: "" -> "This context exists to prove, against a real OpenBao binary in real containers, that the ACME-driven TLS listener works end to end: HTTP-01 and TLS-ALPN-01 challenge solving, privileged and non-privileged port binding, custom cache paths, custom challenge ports, DNS resolution through an injected resolver, and refusal of denied domains. It exists because unit tests cannot exercise CertMagic listener startup, root-privileged port 80/443 binding, Docker port publishing, or DNS-based challenge routing, so the checks run as skipped-by-default external tests gated on a built binary being supplied."
- added `r.acme-listener-configuration` (MUST): "Each scenario declares an additional plain TCP listener with tls_disable true to serve as the ACME directory server and an additional TCP listener with tls_acme_cache_path /tmp and tls_acme_ca_directory pointing at that directory server; the ALPN and non-privileged scenarios additionally set tls_acme_disable_http_challenge true with tls_acme_domains []string{"openbao.dadgarcorp.com"}, and the non-privileged scenario sets tls_acme_alpn_challenge_port 8222 and tls_acme_challenge_host 127.0.0.1 to avoid root."
- added `r.active-node-and-timeout` (MUST): "Each test waits for an active node with testcluster.WaitForActiveNode under a context bounded by a 60 second timeout, requires no error and a non-nil node, and obtains the API client from cluster.ClusterNodes[node].APIClient()."
- added `r.alpn-dns-deny-list` (MUST): "The ALPN scenario installs a DNS resolver on the cluster network for dadgarcorp.com, adds A records for openbao.dadgarcorp.com and invalid.dadgarcorp.com pointing at the container IP, pushes the config, writes pki/config/acme with enabled true and the resolver's remote address, expects certificate acquisition to succeed for openbao.dadgarcorp.com:443 and to fail for invalid.dadgarcorp.com:443."
- added `r.docker-cluster-provisioning` (MUST): "Each test builds DockerClusterOptions against image quay.io/openbao/openbao with tag latest, sets VaultBinary to the value of BAO_BINARY, sets Entrypoint to the result of entrypointPath, uses one core, and passes TRACE log level plus the scenario's AdditionalListeners into VaultNodeConfig, then starts the cluster with docker.NewTestDockerCluster and defers cluster.Cleanup."
- added `r.entrypoint-path-resolution` (MUST): "entrypointPath derives the Docker entrypoint from the calling source file using runtime.Caller(0) and joins the file's directory with ../../../../.release/docker/docker-entrypoint.sh; when runtime.Caller reports not ok it logs that it is assuming a path and returns the same relative path unresolved."
- added `r.non-privileged-dns-routing` (MUST): "The non-privileged scenario points the openbao.dadgarcorp.com A record at the container gateway IP so the ACME server reaches the listener through Docker's host 443 to container 8443 mapping."
- added `r.pki-self-hosting-setup` (MUST): "setupPki mounts a pki secrets engine with 16h default and 32h max lease TTL and allowed response headers Last-Modified, Replay-Nonce, Link and Location, writes pki/config/cluster with both path and aia_path set to http://127.0.0.1 followed by the scenario's ACME port plus /v1/pki, enables pki/config/acme, generates an internal EC root named root with common name "Root R1", and returns the generated certificate string."
- added `r.root-privilege-per-scenario` (MUST): "The privileged and ALPN scenarios set Root true so the container can bind ports 80 and 443, while the non-privileged scenario sets Root false and instead publishes container port 8443 as host port 443 through PublishPorts."
- added `r.skip-without-binary` (MUST): "Every test function other than the helpers reads the BAO_BINARY variable through api.ReadBaoVariable and calls t.Skip with the message "only running docker test when $BAO_BINARY present" when that variable is empty, so the suite is a no-op unless a built binary path is supplied."
- added `r.tls-verification-container` (MUST): "validateTLS builds and runs an Alpine image containing curl with the expected root certificate written to /root.pem, joins it to the cluster's container network, optionally rewrites /etc/resolv.conf with a search domain of dadgarcorp.com and the supplied nameserver, then runs curl --verbose --cacert /root.pem against https://<address>/v1/sys/health and fails the test when the command's non-zero return code disagrees with the expectFail argument."

### third-party-openbao-internal-vault-external-tests-token

- intent: "" -> "This context exists to keep the OpenBao token behavior verified against a real running core rather than against mocks. The two files are the external, black-box test layer for the token store: they mount real backends, authenticate real clients, and assert on API responses, lease counts, and token counts. Anyone changing token creation, orphan handling, entity binding, identity policy composition, CIDR restrictions, revocation-on-startup behavior, standby invalidation timing, or batch token lifecycle must expect these tests to be the contract that breaks first."
- added `r.batch-parent-lease-revoke` (MUST): "TestBatchToken_ParentLeaseRevoke creates a batch token from a leased parent credential and fails unless revoking the parent lease makes the batch token unusable."
- added `r.batch-token-basics` (MUST): "TestBatchTokens configures the cluster with the kv leased passthrough logical backend and the approle credential backend, mounts kv, writes a leased secret and a read-only policy, then creates, looks up and renews tokens and asserts the batch token type behavior exposed by consts."
- added `r.batch-token-roles` (MUST): "TestTokenStore_Roles_Batch covers token roles whose tokens are issued as batch tokens and asserts the resulting token type and role-derived policies."
- added `r.cidr-blocks` (MUST): "TestTokenStore_CIDRBlocks exercises token creation with bound CIDR blocks and asserts the request from inside and outside the bound ranges succeeds or is denied accordingly."
- added `r.cluster-harness` (MUST): "Every test builds its own in-memory cluster with vault.NewTestCluster using vaulthttp.Handler and vault.TestClusterOptions, calls cluster.Start(), defers cluster.Cleanup(), and waits for the first core to become active with vault.TestWaitActive before issuing API calls."
